Recourse is one of my favourite games so far. Its gameplay is unique and offers a lot of different puzzles so the player doesn't get bored while progressing. First of all, I highly recommend you to try the free demo as it shows how your computer runs it and what kind of a game Recourse is!
For the keyboard + mouse configuration, controls are smooth and working. I haven't used a controller while playing this, so I don't know how well they work. I've been satisfied with my own controls, however. I also like that player is able to switch between 1st person and 3rd person views as they like, so those who prefer either can choose and not be bound to whatever the developers have chosen. The developer's Youtube channel also has videos on Recourse, I recommend to check them out too.
When it comes to the story, it's mostly covered by the conversations between Sleet, who's your player character, and Floe as you progress through levels, but it works since it not only gives you information on what has happened, but also builds up what kind of characters Sleet and Floe are. In the beginning, you find yourself from an unknown place and proceed to find out where you are and why.
In the gameplay, there are three different kinds of stages: Puzzle stages, Wave Rush stages and Payload stages. Puzzle stages, as can be suspected from the name, are progressed by solving puzzles with a variety of mechanics, and I have enjoyed them; while they are not too difficult to repel beginners, I never found them too easy to bore me, especially since certain opened doors etc. remain open after finishing the stage and thus don't force the player to redo them when returning to the stage later. Later on in the game and especially when looking for question marks and achievements such as easter eggs they do challenge as the player learns to use what they have.
Wave Rush levels are about fighting enemies known as failbots and gather failbot drives to open up doors in the stage and exchange for waves that can be used for upgrades for Floe. Just like Puzzle levels and Payload levels, these levels also have question marks to be found to use for upgrades.
In Payload levels, you escort a wagon through its route while erasing obstacles from its way and beating failbots, thus earning failbot chips that need to be deposited into the wagon before the time runs out and the wagon closes up for the rest of the stage - more time can be acquired on the stage, so there is space for exploring the stage to find question marks and exploring without risking the time running out. Any chips deposited into the wagon are carried out of the level to be used for upgrades.
TL;DR: I haven't tried out co-op nor controllers, so those are for other players to tell if they work well. However, for what I've experienced, I have nothing to complain about the except that it requires quite a quite powerful computer to play it with a decent FPS especially on high settings. The story is interesting and well executed, gameplay is smooth and movement free, and the game looks great and pleasant, plus the colors are colorblind-friendly. In addition to that all, the game doesn't take much space and is thus fast to download. The demo is perfect for testing the game before choosing to buy it. :)
Pros:
-Nice idea
-Works well
-The colors are pleasant and nothing hurts my eyes + colorblind-friendliness
-Nice puzzles that make the player use their brains
-Intriguing story that is executed well via the conversations
-The main characters are very good
-Smooth controls
-Small file size
-A lot to see and find
-In my own experience the developers have been active and helpful on Steam's discussions on Recourse
-The possibility to switch between 1st person and 3rd person views
Cons:
-It's a heavy game for the hardware

I'll preface by saying that, at the moment, I don't really feel this game is quite worth its asking price; but if you asked me there are very few games I'd say can justify a $40 pricetag. The game doesn't have enough content nor does it feel quite polished enough for what it wants but the devs are active and constantly updating so that could change in the future.
As a puzzle game, this game is... not too hard, really. The puzzles get bigger more than they get trickier, though the later puzzle levels (8 and on) can certainly provide a decent mental workout. But there's definitely a decent bit of variety, up to continuing to introduce elements even in the last levels of the game. And it does feel like every type of puzzle the game presents is developed about as far as it can be, though there are certainly a few that overstay their welcome. There's a nice feeling of progression throughout though, each level is an interconnected hub of smaller puzzles and picking apart one piece unlocks two more, the real joy is finding the ways all the separate pieces interact with each other to get the secret pickups, honestly.
The combat is... a bit weak honestly, since it's all indirect. You throw deployables that do the fighting for you, at least until you unlock the bonus weapon waaayyy near the end of the game that is. There are really only two or three weapons worth using out of the eight available. And the enemies tend to be an annoyance more than a threat. Death is pretty cheap, either just sending you back to a checkpoint with no penalty or dropping all your collected items in the wave rush and payload levels but allowing you to pick up half of them again, and if you're playing it smart you don't keep a large stash anyways. The wave rush levels in particular feel just a bit unnecessary since the combat is never a strong point, but there's few of them and technically you can finish them all in seconds if you want to. The payload levels are a nice change of pace, there's a time limit but not a very strict one and it's easy to extend it as well. I dig this level style a lot more than the wave rush levels. And I do admire that there's diversity in level types, showing off different aspects of the game. The optional race things that appear in every level are another nice little bonus though there's no incentive to beat the best time and trying to do so tends to be the only real source of frustration in the game.
Where the game really works best is in its movement, which is kept consistently fast allowing you to travel large distances with little hassle. And there's even little quirks of the game engine you're expected to discover and exploit a few times. Movement in this game just feels fun, though if you had to be really precise with it I'm sure it'd wear off, but it's distinctly different for a puzzle game. The other aspect of the game that's particularly memorable is the dialogue between the two main characters, which I enjoyed a lot more than I expected to honestly. There's an air of mystery to the overarching plot that plays well into the conversations, a lot of "AI not understanding humans" bits that develop into some serious snark towards humanity by the end and plenty of genuinely funny quips. And there's just, so many dialogues too, I haven't even found them all yet I'm sure, even with how much I have found. There's also some nice little easter eggs tucked away that you can get near the end, they're pretty fun to hunt for and decently clever.
The game also looks pretty solid visually though the game's aesthetic is a bit limited, it kind of wears off after a number of hours playing. And the soundtrack is nice for what it is but definitely a bit restricted, since it's the same set of songs playing on loop for the entirety of the game. You'll probably have them all memorized by the time you beat the game. I eventually just turned the music off and used my own music to stop from going insane.
It's definitely a pretty good game but I wouldn't say it's a great one. Regardless I definitely enjoyed playing it and I would recommend it... on sale.

The game is a puzzle game in its nature. You play as Sleet, after a few puzzles you meet up with another robot Ai Floe. So far the story has been great, dialog is fun and keeps at least myself interested in more of the character's interactions.
Puzzles consist of a lot of smaller things, exploring is a big part of each puzzle area in fact.
Puzzles can range from having X buttons pressed, to Less than X press, or More than X pressed. To finding Y object to put within a machine. Some puzzles are small math tests where you do things like use weights that are between 100 xxx 1000. They use this in other places, even with fire, and electricity.
As you progress you get deployables. These are miniture devices you can toss out about 12 or so before they start imploding. These range from saw blades, lasers that rotate, fires, tesla probe. To things with A. to B. icons (haven't used everything yet.)
Along side normal puzzles you have (actually forgot the name) combat rooms. These have puzzles in them, but to get access to them you have to kill enemy bots and gain money to open more of the stage.
The third type of puzzle room I have witnessed is a sort of escort mission, you have a timer, and a device that moves while near it. You have to figure the whole thing out while staying close to the device to keep it moving.
Over all, movement is very fun and insanely fluid. Decent enough settings. Even a 00:00 - 24:00 day light system you get to play with in the settings, want it pitch black set it to midnight. Want a bright day? Set it too noon.
Like I said in my short review. Only major complaint so far is that while it has controller support you can not invert the Y axis at all. (yet, dev already comment saying it would be in the next patch or so)
My experience so far, well worth 40 bucks and I just scratched the surface.
Another thing I forgot to note here. EVERY stage has a way point race on it. Even the combat, and payload missions!

Basically to people reading this, ESO is an MMORPG of Elder Scrolls in around the 2nd Era, the goal of the game is different to person to person, but you are intended to defeat the daedric prince known as Molag Bal (You know the guy who gives you that cool looking mace in previous TES games) and basically you will.
PROS:

CONS:

Slime Rancher is a game created by Monomi Park, a new game studio (comprised of two people during development, which has now to four people) with Slime Rancher being their very first game. The game follows a Life-Simulation format where you play as Beatrix LeBeau, a girl from Earth who has travelled to a distant planet known as The Far Far Range to begin life as a 'Slime Rancher': someone who looks after many different types of Slimes on their Ranch by collecting them across the Range, and then collecting their plorts after feeding them to sell on the market back to Earth as they use these plorts as resources. Sounds simple, right? Well, for a first time game, let's see how it holds up:
. The game looks absolutely beautiful with all the different enviroments giving off a different feel and atmosphere that makes them a joy to go through.
. A healthy amount of slime types with different attributes and abilities, which can make them unoredictible and adds to the challenge and fun of having them on your Ranch. Plus they're just the most ADORABLE things you will ever see in a video game.
. A decent amount of upgrades and abilites for Beatrix. From increased health and storage space so you can hold more of any one item (up to 100 of 1 item when fully upgraded), to a water cannon and a jetpack to make traversal easier.
. The 'Slime Science' gadgets is a very welcome addition to the game. From digging in certain areas for rare items, to actually making teleporters which make traversing to a particular place much easier. Or you can just make decorations to liven up your ranch.
. The gameplay is very addictive and can be a lot of fun.
. Diverse locations from lush forests to barren deserts which are all plenty of fun to explore.
. Lots of secerts to find, from giant 'Gordo' Slimes which, when burst from feeding it enough, can uncover special keys to unlock other areas, as well as teleporters to secert areas of the ranch, to lootable pods which can contain rare items and new Slime Science gadgets. This all helps to successfully encourage exploration.
. Other than the 5-Day Rush (which is see how much money you can get in just 5 days), there is no real challenge in this game. Yes the game is not easy, and feral slimes (slimes that attack you on sight unless fed) can make traversing a little tedious, but it lacks any real difficulty, and can become a breeze once you know what you're doing. hopefully with the new updates coming, it will add a bit more of a challenge to the game.
. The game can be a real grind at times to get the right upgrades or gadgets, with the 7Zee club (this game's version of a 'level up' system) being the main culprit. whilst fine on the early levels, later levels with really useful upgrades will require obsurd amounts of money to unlock. And yes whilst the pay off is really good, the journey to get there can be a real slog sometimes.
. Whilst not much of a problem now thanks to there being a 'Safe Mode' which you can choose before booting the game up, I encounted a plethera of game breaking glitches and bugs with the mode off. As far as I know this is only a problem on PC, and yes the Safe Mode does help, but having to switch to this mode shows the game's poor optimisation on PC and it can be a hassle
. The gamplay can get slightly repeatitive due to not having that much variety in gameplay. Again, not that much of a problem due to how addicting it is.
. You only have a maximum of 4 inventory slots (with an extra slot for the water cannon), and there's no way to upgrade it. This is far too small for how much you can collect.
The game's lack of difficulty, bugs, and small amounts of grinding at certain points is made up for by it's gorgeous locations, fun and addiciting (yet slightly repeatitive) gameplay, a healthy amount of things to find, do and explore, and its beautiful and adorable charm which make it an absolute joy to play. Whilst not perfect, this game is absolutely amazing, especially considering how many people made it. For a first time game, Monomi Park have made an out-of-nowhere hit that makes it one of the most enjoyable games of 2017.

You can choose to upgrade your skills and there are stacks of skills to upgrade in addition to that there's lots of hacking to do and loads of freaks to kill.
Being stealthy is very important in your style of gameplay because if you just rush headlong into some areas of the game the turrets will take you out.
Another very important thing to remember is that if the cameras spot you the alarm systems will go crazy and if that happens then you can almost be overrun by (The Many), but once the alarm system resets then the onslaught subsides,
You also have the option of choosing what style of play you want to start with and this is based on the career that you choose after you have been through basic and advanced training.
Another point about the game that I really like is that you have to maintain your weapons repairing them otherwise they start to jam and can become useless.
You can also upgrade your skills in this area of the game as well.
You can play the game on one of several different difficulty levels and the harder the level the more scarce things become, things like ammo, nanites and cyber modules etc.
So if you really like a challenge try it out on hard mode and oh yes there is also an impossible mode.
You should spend some serious time playing System Shock 2 it's a great game and you will have a tremendous time, trust me, Insect.

System Shock 2 is the grandfather of modern FPS shooters. Despite it being quite underrated, System Shock 2 was the influence behind games like Bioshock and Half-Life. It is a dark and gritty game that combines a dark and scary atmosphere with surprisingly enjoyable exploration, crafting and research.
As far as the story goes, you start out as a recruit and get to select your main path of game style. You have the Marines which will eventually allow you to get your hands on weapons ranging from pistols to grenade launchers and EMP rifles. You have the Navy, the "tech" class which makes it easier to hack machines and security systems. The last path is the OSA, which specialises in 'psi-powers' which allow you to use your mind to attack enemies, move items and objects from a distance and disable cameras. Afterwards, you are given a selection of three 'subpaths' which give you points in specific skills. Afterwards, you can level up your skills using cybermodules which are generally given to you as a reward for completing missions but you may find them in the world. Players are not restricted to the class they chose e.g those who picked the Marine path can invest their cybermodules in PSI powers. While a "jack of all trades" approach is tempting, it is best to stick to your chosen path because you may find it become incredibly expensive to maintain skill trees at the same time.

When you're finished, the game begins. You find yourself onboard the Von Braun, a ship which has succumbed to a strange infection. All hell has broken loose and you must save yourself from the hybrids and other alien lifeforms, and from the psychotic Artificial Intelligence known as XERXES.
The player can paint a picture of what happened to the Von Braun through collectibles, which are often recordings made by other crew members. Much like in Bioshock, they also may contain important passcodes and give away locations of important items. Through this method, following the story is optional and all those simply wanting to beat the game do not have to concentrate while a NPC goes on and on. (In this game, the only NPCs who talk to you are SHODAN and whatshernameagain.)
System Shock 2 has some of the best level design I've ever seen, and some of the worst. Backtracking is one of the biggest issues this game has. While the levels are big and non-linear allowing for player freedom, they encourage backtracking. As you continue through the game, you are able to explore the Von Braun fully. An elevator located on every floor of the Von Braun allows you to return to an already explored floor (for the purposes of research, farming, healing etc.) What makes the level design superb is that it gives the player not only a sense of discovery and exploration, it also gives the player a sense of confusion and being lost. Some levels contain branches where you have to explore them, find an item and return to the main "hub" part to accomplish a mission to progress further. This does often lead to a sense of misdirection. This is something System Shock 2 does good. That being said, some levels basically have major chokeholds which don't allow the player to use different strategies if an enemy is blocking them.
Every level contains security cameras monitored by the rogue AI XERXES. If it spots you, it will activate a security alarm which essentially sends a horde of enemies at you. It is always vital to watch your surroundings.
Combat wise, the game offers a large arsenal of weaponry. Guns, grenade launchers, sabres and many more. Of course most weapons require a specific level in that particular skill line (e.g EMP Rifle requires an energy skill of 6.) As I mentioned earlier, the player is given the freedom to invest in the weapons skill tree even if they picked the Navy or OSA.
Every weapon is degradable and you have to repair it if it becomes broken. While this degradable feature does make it substantially difficult for the player if they don't monitor their weapon's level of quality, it can be a bit annoying at times. The player can also modify their weapons using the modify skill, which basically increases the stats of that particular weapon.
Combat aside, another unique feature of System Shock 2 is Research. On your journey, you may come across an item that is 'unresearched.' To research it, you require a table, and the required chemicals. To get these chemicals, you have to go to a chemical storeroom, which are located in almost every map. However, each chemical storeroom is not identical and you may to have to explore until you find the storeroom with the chemical you need. Upon researching an item, it will tell you what it does. For instance, some enemies may drop one of these items. If researched, it gives you a % damage boost against that particular enemy. While researching objects is an optional feature. It is best to invest in researching, as enemies later on do become difficult and the boost would help.
Present in System Shock 2 is a hacking system, where you have to click on squares to create a line. Hacking is used to open crates, hack machines and disable security systems as well as terminating security alarms.
System Shock 2 also offers a variety of enemies, ranging from psychic monkeys to annelid spiders and giant robots. As the game progresses, you have to face a growing variety of enemies. It does get incredibly difficult later on. Each encounter with enemies rests on the path you have chosen before. Marines can simply charge in, wreck the enemy and let that be the end of that. A Navyman can backtrack and find a way to avoid the enemy, and a OSA can use their PSI powers to stealthy kill the enemy. Enemies are generally randomly placed on the map, (apart from some pre-set robots.)
Levels are not saturated in enemies, and there are times when the map can be empty. This gives the player plenty of freedom to explore, and makes each encounter with enemies unique. As the player progresses, enemy difficulty increases substantially. This difficulty can be eventually lowered through research. It does not matter what weapons you have, you will always be underpowered. You have to be incredibly observant of your surroundings, and this is something that System Shock 2 does very well.
Present in this game is a co-op mode, which allows you to play with two other people! I strongly recommend that you finish System Shock 2 solo before playing co-op, because playing with a partner is a different experience. Knowing that you have backup deducts from the game's overall atmosphere. Co-op, although it is generally stable and bugfree, does contain some issues. (Not surprising for a game made in 1999.) I have encountered some bugs and glitches such as: unnoticable lag where automatic doors open for the host and not for the other players. The elevator can get stuck and won't change the level essentially trapping you (this can be fixed by all players restarting the game.) Enemies can [rarely] get stuck in their default model (aka 'mingebag' ) position and not do anything apart from making noise. A friend and I also encountered a glitch where NPCs would spawn in places they're not supposed to be. (We encountered some live crew member NPCs on one of the decks.) If playing co-op, i would save right before the SHODAN room (Most glitches tended to start after this scene in my case.) Apart from this, Co-op is fun to play with friends.
On one final note, the atmosphere in this game is excellent in making the player feel weak and underpowered. While the game's music is topnotch quality, it doesn't always fit in with the feel of the game. Regardless, the dark, gritty and scary environments keep the player awake and observant. Just remember to keep in mind that this game was made in 1999 as the graphics have not aged well.
System Shock 2 is a must-play for Halflife and Bioshock fans. It combines a range of unique aspects and abilities. it is an underrated yet enjoyable experience.

BE WARNED: this game is not your normal zombie appocoliptic game. you need to relearn a lot of stuff.
L4D is not comparable here. ammo is rare, and zombies are tough, and you will die... a lot.
This game is more realistic than a lot of these things on the market everything from ammo rarity to heavy melee weapons to infections. All with a creepy depressing atmosphere to boot.
But that was the elevator pitch lets break it down.
I now its not a 1 to  1 comparision but lets look at 2 other games L4D2 and Dead Rising 2 (DR2) for comparisons.
Now I want to just say I love both L4D2 and DR2 for what they are and can endorse them full heartedly, but I feel this game fills a different nieche
Story: 4/5
A perfect blend of background information and voices but never a needed requirement. So many zombie games have stories that are as follows. You are a a survivor get through this area to your goal for extraction. This game has this element as well. And you may ignore the story all together. but Its there. In the hold out mission you often hear military troops on radios explain that BY LAW you need to hold your ground to earn your rescue. That is terrifying. That means the national security of (undisclosed country (the game never says but it does not hurt it either)) has uterly failed in its job to protect the people. And in the event based mission the story still holds. You are trying to get to your evac, but you hear things over communications. People willing to help, and others keeping track of you. But you also hear them fail. So the story is a little cleache, but it still puts in effort where a lot of games just say why bother.
Gameplay: 4/5
Fair but brutal. It will punish you. The controls work fine, but if you mess up it is your fault. Every mission is winable, without question. but you need to be aware of a lot of things. Not an impossible number but still just like in a semi real situation you need to focus on your surroudings. Weigh options of risk and reward. Yes there is ammunition over there, right behind the three zombies. Is it worth it, well that is your call. The game often rewards if not demands you not use the run and gun mentality of kill everything in your path. I appreciate this idea. I do enjoy the Constant mayhem of L4D2 and DR2's general mentality of dice up everything you can, but it is also equally emportant to sometimes remember that in a more realistic situation you will not come across hundreds if not thousands of rounds of military grade ammunition and firepower the decision to make the game more focused on the reality of making EVERY bullet count is a nice take. Once my friend and I were playing and I grabbed a shotgun. and I am a scrouge with bullets (not a hoarder i would call out anything that was not my shells to him and constatly ask if he needs this or that as well as my other team mates) and at one point I had aquired about 34 shells. My friend the party and I all were just blown away at my luck. I was god for a few moments. But We all knew that I could not waste a single one of those shots becasue between our group and the exit was about 300 plus undead. so yeah No mater what you feel like you are not the upper force. which brings us to...
Mood / tone / atmosphere: 5/5
Oh god they nailed every second of this. I can't play this game to destress, because it is like a real zombie appocolypse. There is no break or end, there is only the endless stream of flesh pounding against your positions and your mind. The only sigh of relefe that is ever heard is when either someone pulls of a major stunt to save their lives and at the end of a mission. The music is somber. The enemy is not agressive in the normal sence, more just a force that is in your way. And you just get the feeling that you might not get out of this one alive.
Graphics: 3/5
Average. Nothing special. But considering this is a free game and there are no massive screwups I'll give them a break. I've seen a lot worse done on a lot bigger projects so don't complain much.
Community: range 2/5 - 5/5 with an average of 4/5
They are often kind and forgiving (unlike the game) They will try to help new players and often fogive mistakes, so long as the person is trying to learn. The issue is the low end does exist and for new players and old players they are an annoyance. Often it takes the shape of some kid throwing a tantrum if they get killed for some reason (even if it is their fault) or they don't get a gun (even though they chew through bullets with one kill then complain that they don't have any then demand another gun)  or a specific weapon (I got kicked once because i grabbed a wrench in front of me that someone wanted. They punched me then banned me.) But as I said these are the Rare cases on the whole more people play this with a sence of team mentalities. and I try to be in that group.
Potentail for moments: 4/5
(This is the possibility for funny / bad♥♥♥♥♥/ or humbling moments)
Yeah given how open-ish this game is moment will occure. I once was in an alley way with exactly one survivor. We were the last two. He said over the mic, "want to know the funniest things," I knew what he was about to say. "I'm infected" I gave him a blast of a shotgun. He was kidding but this moment was very intense.
At another moment I made a last stand. I was infected. My party was being chased by a hoard. I knew I had maybe another minute to live. I told my party to move ahead. I stopped emptied two mags of 9 MM rounds into the swarm dropping one with each shot then took out a grenade I had been saving and cooked it in my hand. As I was overrun It went off and I took out a good chunk of the swarm and my would be super zombie in one last moment.
The last story I have was one of comedy. My party had gone a long way. Secretly I was infected and kept downing large numbers of pills to not turn. We got to the evac sight. We won, but moments before we won I turned. My group saw me drop then the screen said we escaped. We all just started cracking up realizing most likely the Safe zone we got delivered to was turned into the undead by us. (of course that did not happen, but its more just timing)
So yeah memories will follow.
Overall rating: 4.5/5
The game is really the first game I felt truely was a FTP without trying to con people. TF2 is a close second, but this game delivers so much to the players without asking for anything in return. It creates a realistic(ish) zombie appocolypse where you are not the one man army that so many other games build you up to be. You are just a person trying to not die. The gameplay, atmosphere, and story all set up one of my favorite games.
I recommend this game to anyone who has time to kill. It's a great game worth playing.

[THIS REVIEW DOES CONTAIN SPOILERS]
After all of the negative reviews I've seen for this game, I'd never think that I would enjoy myself playing this more than the original dishonored, which is one of my most played stealth games on steam, but somehow I did.
I praise the decision in bringing back characters such as Delilah into the series, as I loved the Dishonored 1 DLCs Brigmore Witches and Knife Of Dunwall, both for attention to detail and character development, as you explore new areas from a completely new perspective. I did feel as if Delilah did deserve more time in development and this game was more than enough to satisfy this. The antagonist Delilah is fleshed out spectacularly throughout this story, along with some of my favourite twists to the dishonored franchise so far Delilah is Jessamine's sister who was cast out of the tower and left to poverty, with the false promise of the throne, and Meegan Foster being Billie Lurk.
The developers really upped their game in terms of their level creativity. A few that stand above include levels such as the Jindosh Mansion, a house filled with walking death traps, levers and puzzles, all while being disturbingly watched by the Grand Inventor as he detects your every move. It's challenging, complex, atmosphere, intense and in my eyes, one of the best designs for a Dishonored theme, Closely followed by maybe The Flooded District, which was one of my favourite settings through both of these games.
I feel as if life in the city was highly improved, with the idea of more civilian conversation, more areas where people could lay low, along with more dilemmas such as wreckages, abandoned homes etc. This was a large improvement from Dishonored 1 as while it did have some social dilemmas, it doesn't compare to 2. Along with being able to hear different opinions of situations going around them, for example, the two woman discussing the speech of the overseer during the Addermire mission.
While I did find the voice acting of The Outsider to be a strange change, I got used to it around the 7th Mission and was able to see his effort in filling the role was well done. However, in terms of the Protagonist, while I do find the addition of the character being able to give input on a situation, I feel like sometimes it was unnecessary, but I found it to be satisfying during story based events rather than minor things such as Object Activation, such as globes.
Also, small things such as glass panes and objects being more of an obstacle really helps with the realism of stealth and also makes you think before you decide to far reach straight into a window and think you're gonna be silent.
I was able to run this game with my 750ti and my Intel G3258 at low settings with the addition of max textures, for details and such, and was able to keep an fps of around 45-60, with the exception of getting close to gravehounds, which would affect it severely, but not for long. Overall I would give this game an 8/10, I would be more inclined to give a 9, if it were not for some glitches concerning certain power combos like domino and the affects you put with it, along with some glitches concerning detection when loading into a game, but sometimes with enemies detecting you almost instantly, even if they have not seen you once.

So right off the bat I'll admit that I had a lot of time for the first game warts and all. There were definitely some issues with the first entry, sometimes enemies could be pretty cheap and the controls could be frustrating. Having said that it's also true that I enjoyed the throwback tank style controls because I absolutely adore old school survival horror games.
This sequel does an excellent and surprising job of tightening things up nicely and also introduces some much needed fleshing out of Sebastian's character. Whilst I enjoyed his glib and painfully obvious remarks in the first game he's much more engaging this time around. He's hardly got the depth of a character from The Wire or something but he's very much improved.
I actually appreciated the story in the first game more so than many other's seemed to but this one makes a lot more sense and feels quite personal which always gives the leading character a much more relatable drive. I will say the game is probably a bit less scary than the first one. The grimy environments and gastly enemy design felt a bit more nerve shredding however the more open world nature of this game adds an element of paranoia into the mix as the open spaces make you feel extremely vulnerable especially when the enemy count and threat ramps up. You'll find yourself desperate for the sanctuary of a safe house to get you off the hair raising streets.
The game has a great arch and without throwing any spoilers out there it feels very fulfilling and the antagonists are suitably twisted if a little 'camp horror' feeling but it doesn't feel out of place tonally given the nature of this franchise.
PERFORMANCE:
Now this is a mixed bag. If your chosen resolution is 1080p as long as you have something approaching a GTX 1070 and possibly a 1060 you should be able to max things out at around 60fps although there have been reports of stuttering and other issues so your millage may vary.
1440p 60fps will require a gtx 1070 or a 1080.
4k is where things get a bit sticky. Even on the lowest settings I couldn't reach 60 fps on my 1080. I decided to settle on 4k ultra settings with a 30fps cap. I've found the game feels smooth and benefits from the increased image quality. The world is quite attractive and the game doesn't feel as sluggish as you might think at this frame rate given the style of game.
All in all I'd unreservedly recommend this game to anyone. If you're into horror its a fun romp if a little lacking in 'Silent Hill' levels of unease. If you're not into horror then this is still going to be a fun thrilling experience.

This is an ambitious, deeply, deeply flawed game. It applies roughly similar mechanics to the original, and mixes things up by adding a somewhat open world to the mix. But this open world is more like the one found in Silent Hill Downpour, a game of equal ambition, yet also of even deeper flaws. The basic game loop works, until it doesn't. This is less of a horror title, and much more of a stealth game. Playing without avoiding zombies and shanking them in the back is how this works. Pretty much the only way out of a multi-zombie encounter is running away. If the game allows that. Occasionally the stealth mechanics are switched off. Which highlights the superbly wonky combat mechanics. While wonky combat mechanics are usually a feature of horror games, here it means that a zombie that is in striking distance cannot be hit with a handgun due to the way aiming works. So keeping a distance is vital. But also not always possible.
Overall, the game is clunky, creaky and filled with odd design choices. The player character cannot surmount any obstacle that does not prompt "LS+A to climb". There are also plenty of invisible walls in odd places, especially handy in boss fights. Enemies get stuck in the environment a lot, especially bigger ones. Which is especially great when those are meant to be snuck by.
The plot is a mess. The beginning reveals that everything takes place in some sort of virtual reality, which - at least for me - robs the game of most horror there is. Weird things happen all the time, but it can all be shrugged off as "well, it's all VR, so that's that?" The main character's motivation is essentially a fridged daughter. The first main villain sits in that part of the camp-serious spectrum that neither really works. He comes across as mainly uninspired, not really threatening and mostly just dumb, video gamey in the worst sense of the word.
The game does have its fun moments. The creature design is nice, and there are parts that do feel rewarding to conquer. But overall the negatives far outweigh the positives. While the creatures are wonderfully grisly, the environments lack variation and are for the most part just ugly and uninspired. The first 12 hours of the game consist of a drab open world town and equally drab, linear corridors. After that the palette is switched up a bit, but that comes way too late.
Overall this is a MUCH worse game than the original. While the first game was also somewhat clunky and lacking polish, the sequel is much worse in that regard. It shows that Mikami is not directing. This game lacks inspiration and good ideas that would keep it afloat for more than the first 8 hours, after which it quickly overstays it's welcome. I would recommend to avoid this and search for scares elsewhere this Halloween season.

MatrixMuse’s review of
Slime Rancher
I will start by saying it was Jim Sterling's review that got this game on my list. So a thank you to him, and his honest two videos on the game.
Categories seeing each game needs to be addressed by its own strength and faults. I can’t really compare a single player game to the same categories I would a MMO or Co-Op Game. This review is based off of seventeen hours of gameplay, completing 26 / 57 achievements.
Overview - So very cute, a fight against the inevitable Tarr.
Gameplay
There is not a ton of controls, the tooltip does its job in telling you what is what. I enjoyed this game very much, and still do as I am going to continue playing it. Now i will say I did break out Google and look stuff up. The loading screen tips, pass by way too fast for me to read. Not for any of the puzzles, my days of being a GM prepared me for whatever this game has to offer. Though some quarks are just something I had to look up, now good news there is a great Wiki out there to help with all of the questions.
Pros
It’s so damned cute, with its cat slimes, and its cute noises as they play. Now you don’t have to understand it but, I hate chickens. It is not a casual hate, it is the same hate people feel when they squish a spider. A game where I can toss chickens into a slime pin so my Hunter slims will eat it, is a pro.
I feel rewarded for exploration. It is wonderful to find new places and explore. The random boxes are all over the place. Now I am not yet at the end and likely have a few more doors and end game (Vaults) to experience.
Crafting system is not bad. Now break out that Wiki we have crafting. It is not hard to level it up nore is it hard to get materials for. There was some critical information i was missing, and it is you can put collectors out in the world. Not just on your farm. In fact you have to to get some of the materials.
Story
There is a story here, just take a moment to read stuff. There are markers in the world they kinda look like Hyperion H’s (Borderlands reference). Read them they are interesting, also you get mail, from a few people in the story. Now is it riveting? No not really your a farmer, in the end of the day your filling food bins and shoveling ‘Plorts’ for money.
Cons
Now there are a few things that have me sighing in this game. Now my years of video game playing has me at an advantage. I don’t need the map, in fact it was not until my husband looked over my shoulder and went. “Oh I would get so lost” Did I even look for a map function (M Key).
It can get a tad, Farmville feeling. With Rancher in the name I expected this. Slimes need food, without food they become sad, cranky, or in the case of Quantum slimes, just leave their pin and look for food. The balance of what kind of slimes you start with has to be balanced with what resource you can get and how much of it you need. Having Cat slimes to early on can mean disaster if you can’t yet afford chick hutch.
Nutural
Have to go into this not thinking too big, knowing pink plorts are in abundance just out the door. Let them eat in the wild and collect what is there.Now this can be even more taxing realizing you need double tall walls, or your slims just jump out, and a sky net. So before you can even house slimes you are tossing down 1500 in coins. Not including having food on hand for what you put in that house.
Water kills Tarr. There I said it, just incase you are saddened by seeing Tarr’s rampaging killing all the cute Cat Slimes.
Replay?
I think I could replay this 5 or so times, perhaps do a few things differently. The main reason why there is ‘differently’ at all is well some Largos are hard or impossible to move. Planning out where things would go after knowing what to expect would be a boon.
Overall 8/10

This is endless fun and adventure.

This was my favourite game in 2016. As a preface, I had none of the performance issues experienced by many people, so I cannot comment on that, purely on the game itself when it's running fine. I understand that some people are having trouble even with hardware that should be fine, but on my end I had smooth >60 fps the entire game. Whether I'm just lucky or not I'm not sure, but it worked great for me.
Dishonored 2 really expanded on the story of the first game, and kept the really weird techno-fantasy setting on the first game going strong. The levels are full of intricate things that are so alien yet so consistent that it feels like a believable world, and the Stranger and the Void are always interesting every time it pops up.
As for the gameplay itself, I really liked the way it always felt like I had options. I chose Corvo at the beginning, and mostly played through stealthily, the only kills I got were a couple of unintentional ones where I accidentally left an unconsious guard in a puddle of water, and when an enemy got knocked off the side of a building by my sleep dart. None of the missions pigeonholed me into making a choice I didn't want. Even one mission that at first seemed to require the death of a faction leader eventually opened up to reveal a third option as I looked around the area.
The levels themselves are all great in this regard, always unique from each other and each having all sorts of different ways to get through them depending on what powers and such you're using. Especially noteworthy is the clockwork mansion, which I won't spoil but when it all first starts moving aorund it's just really intersting to get into. At no point during anything did it feel like a chore, and I honestly can't think of any spots in the game I didn't like.
Looking forward to replaying it with Emily and perhaps doing a full-agression run. Highly reccomend provided it runs okay on your computer.

However do to my love of this game and the superb gameplay I'm willing to turn a blind eye for now (especially with the promise of fixes coming soon). Overall I would definitely recommend this to anyone who loved the first game and is looking for more. However if perforamnce at high settings is an absolute must, I'd say hold off until the game is fixed.

System Shock 2 is Bioshock's older, far more badass and brutal brother. I loved Bioshock, Bioshock 2, and to a slightly lesser extent Bioshock Inifinite, and I've gotta say, this 16 YEAR OLD game makes them all look like garbage.
Scratch that, System Shock 2 makes just about every other game look like garbage.
Letting alone the fact the this came out IN 19-♥♥♥♥ING-99, it has a brilliant, immersive story; great equipment and RPG elements, and is scary as all hell. The sole way in which this game shows it's age (aside from the graphics, which i'll discuss in a moment) is in its melee hitting. Sometimes hitting small monsters is kind of annoying. That's It.
Aside from slighgtly dated graphics, which again,  were released in 1999, the game still looks pretty good, and after spending enough time on the Von Braun you'll stop noticing their dated look.
This game does present one problem; after playing it to the end, the influence this game has had on every game that has followed it is STAGGERING, you will become infuriated as you realize your favorite franchises just copied System Shock 2 (inb4 its a sequel, nothing is original. Shut up), like, blatantly. And then the logical conclusion, which is far more infuriating, HOW HAS THERE NOT BEEN MORE GAMES OF THIS QUALITY THIS WHOLE GODDAMN TIME?!?! NINETEEN ♥♥♥♥ING NINETY NINE FOR ♥♥♥♥S SAKE.
If you haven't played it, finish reading this, then seriously, REALLY SERIOUSLY, buy it right ♥♥♥♥ing now and set out aboard the Von Braun. This game will fall into your favorite games of all time, and deserves all the praise and more it has ever received.

I played this for the first time in 2015, and it is still a fantastic game, even without nostalgia. The gameplay and AI are dated, and I would recommend looking for some graphics mods, but even after 16 years this is one of the better games that I've played.
Firstly, the atmosphere in this game is incredible. I could only play in 30-minute spurts for the first few levels, because the game really creeped me out. The audio and sound effects in this game are great and help set the mood. If you've played bioshock(if you haven't you really should), this game is very similar, although it's also a lot scarier than bioshock. After some time playing, you start to get a little used to the constant feeling of fear, but as you progress you encounter more things that are even more unsettling. The audio logs added pieces of the story together as you collect them, and make you wonder what the hell happened on this ship. The atmosphere and story sucks you in, it's so good.
Once you get used to the horror aspects of the game, you start to actually figure out how the game works. This game has a ridiculous amount of customization for you to choose from, but like the rest of the game you are limited in your resources and skill points(called cyber modules). I started out putting points into PSI and ended up using a lightsaber halfway through, using PSI to buff/amplify my melee skills. There are so many ways you can play, and I can easily see this game having a lot of replay value because of it.
And without spoiling anything, the story is great.
TL:DR - Fantastic game, 9/10 mostly because it is a little dated
PROS
-Amazing atmosphere
-Great use of audio
-Interesting story
-Expansive and fun skill system, customizable
-Great setting
-SHODAN
CONS

-Mods make graphics pretty good, but some things like enemy models are still ugly(not a big deal though)
- last minute or so is meh, was expecting an amazing ending after the rest of the game.

verdict: 9/10.  Im so glad i played this game and i will be happy to play it again.  Seems to be so many ways to play this game you could play it 4 times through and not have tried everything.
More depth about the game:
The combat has great diversity.  You get these "cybernetic modules" by completeing tasks or finding them in the environment.  You then spend these on upgrades.  you can specialize in hacking (opening locked creates, turning hostile turrets to fight for you ect), weapon repairing, weapon modifiying (upgrading your weapons damage ect.) or invest in research, some items need a number of research points to be used.  then after all that you can upgrade your strength (inventory size and melee damage) endurance (max health increase, hazard resistance) agility (movement speed, recoil reduction) cybernetic affinity (makes hacking, modifying and repairing easier) psionic ability (which increases the amount of damage you deal with PSI powers).  That reminds me you can also can have these "PSI powers" thats basically magic.  Some weapons have a weapon skill requirement like having cyber modules in standard weapons, energy weapons, heavy weapons or exotic weapons.  This is a♥♥♥♥♥♥load of ways to play the game but due to the games difficulty it kind of forces you to pick 3 of these things and forget the rest.  This does make the game have a high replay value but i really dont like getting locked into a playstyle.  And sense you cant really test if you want standard weapons or energy weapons you could easily get stuck with something you dont like.  Ya you could put points into a little of everything but your inventory will fill FAST and i dont think you could carry all those weapons.  And i couldnt imagine anyone not going into the hacking skill, as half the great stuff you get is locked inside creates.

I've only played Smite a few weeks, here's my impression so far:
PROS:
-Auto-leveling option. You can easily pre-set each ability per level gain, for EACH toon.
-Auto item buying option. I love this! I hate sorting menus & reading long descriptions about virtual hats.
-Characters w/actual stories. All these gods have been around way longer than Sonic & Link.
-Lots of playmodes. I don't even know what the 'main' mode may be, I always play Arena.
-Good tutorials. Actual in-game videos & whatnot.
-Fairly simple item descriptions.
-Lots of skill shots. Way too much stupid-powerful AOE though.
-WASD movement! I hate "click" movement. Literally anything is better than click-moving in an action game...Atari joystick, trakball, anything.
CONS:
-Lots of AFKs.
-Lots of bad players. I mean, people who just walk into enemy base & melt. Then AFK for 5-10 min. There should be a 10 bot game minimum before any PvP is allowed for a new player.
-Even if you play good & buy good items etc, you can still lose horribly due to bad matchmaking. This makes it a roguelike game for me. Obviously, if you have friends to play with, it's better.
-Certain popular gods like Thor, Neith & Ares seem really OP. Ares is like Thresh from LoL, if Thresh could continuously throw his chain & even throw 5 at once. Worst of all, the pull has no animation, you just teleport to his side instantly. It also cancels moves like Ullr's E leap, no matter when you use it. Anyway, this is the kind of game-breaking garbage I was trying to get away from in games like LoL/DOTA.
-In general, it seems way more lopsided than LoL/DOTA, where you seem to have at least a chance of making a comeback. In Smite, teams snowball, & I've seen games end 46-0.
I think the game seems pretty amateur in it's present form, will keep my eye on it & update when I can. For now I can only recommend it for overweight children with low standards and/or brain damage.

This is a game that I randomly decided to buy as it was only 47p at time of purchase, and to be honest this game feels like it would be around £6.99 price tag.
Suits: A Business RPG is seriously worth picking up for a fun RPG that lasts around 4 to 5 hours. While I didn't get many of the references/ jokes that were in this game, it kept me going as the plot was personally very interesting (Personally the game felt like earthbound while I was playing through it).
The gameplay is basically Turn based RPG (like Final Fantasy) where you select your character and he can attack the enemy/ boss. The other moves your characters can do are special attacks which use up a bit of your TP (Tech points) or FU (Fuel), which can either buff up your party members or debuff/ attack enemy's. Of course you can also upgrade your party members with equipment and also buy items to use in fights. Personally I enjoyed this style of game play as it allowed me to strategize a plan to beat the enemy or boss, as each one tends to have their own special move which you will need to work around in order to beat them.
The graphics I personally feel set the right mood for the game, as you are in a bleak, desolate world ruled by the corporation. The same applies to music as it is plays in all the battles that you have throughout the game but is rarely playing in the overworld, but it contributes the whole atmosphere of the world that you exist in.
Personally I would give this game a 9/10 overall.

Ok in all seriousness, I picked this game up on a whim, its ridiculously low price sort of helped me feel comfortable picking it up. I'm very glad I did.
Suits a business RPG is a role playing game where you take up the role of a businessman who just graduated from business school. Since cooperations rule the planet in this universe.
For me the humor was on point and reminds me a bit of Rick and Morty, just enough dark humor and unexpected twists in it that makes it funny for me. 4th wall breaking, Easter eggs, and dark humor.
Gameplay wise it reminds me of Earthbound. There is some level grinding and yes there is no free healing, however that is usually how this genre of RPG works. There is some grinding, but I never got tired of it, mostly because I kept wandering around into random peoples' houses.
Usually I don't like bringing up the graphics since that is never the selling point for me, however I think it fits the dystopian 1984 vibe the developers were going for. The hand drawn backgrounds makes the game a bit more memorable in my eyes.
Honestly the best part about this game besides the concept and humor is the exploration. I usually just wander around and loot everything in sight. Which leads me to discover things, I won't spoil anything since playing this game without knowing anything that pops up is satisfying.
Also it is not an Undertale clone, I know my Undertale playtime isn't much, but I have played on another friend's account quite a bit to understand the gameplay and mechanics. They are similar only because of the genre they are in. 2D turn based RPGs. It is like saying every tennis video game ever conceived is a rip off of pong. Or every FPS is a ripoff of Doom. (Note: Undertale is an awesome game, I still highly recommend it, I just saw people calling this game a ripoff.)
My final verdict:
Suits is a good game, although humor is
probably going to fuel most of your enjoyment if you don't like the visuals or gameplay. So Suits isn't for everyone, but it is very lowly priced so honestly it is worth a shot. Plus steam refund exists now if you really really don't like the game that much.
Pros:
Good humor
Nice visuals
Interesting concept
Exploration
Good sound (when there is any)
Isn't an Undertale ripoff like many people seem to think.
Cons:
Lack of sound
Grinding
Can be difficult for newcomers to the genre.
9/10

Take this review from someone who played on Nightmare difficulty and really enjoyed the first game.
Pros:
+More personal story
+Better characterization
+Improved graphics (it has gorgeous shadows and lighting effects)
+Combat is still as satisfying
+Lengthy story
+Improved stealth mechanics
+There are wide-open levels
+The wide-open levels have some surprises that tie into the story, so be sure to explore
+Cool bosses
+Runs pretty well on my old FX-6350 CPU and GTX 970 GPU. (Mostly ultra settings at 40-50 FPS)
+Has genuinely terrifying set pieces
Note how I say wide-open levels because this is not an open-world game. There are just levels that are surprisingly expansive.
Cons:
-Voice acting is a bit wooden at times
-Different voice actors (but they do grow on you)
-Sebastian is still a bit awkward to control especially with the new cover system
-Some of the dialogue is awkward
-Villains could be more developed
-Bosses aren't as memorable compared to the first game's bosses
-Side missions aren't very interesting
-Enemy AI is dumb and completely exploitable
-Stealth kill upgrades make the game too easy
Overall, this is a great game if you love Japanese horror, or just horror in general. It's a big improvement on the first game in terms of optimization, story, gameplay, and graphics. Although stealth killing makes many parts of the game easy, there is still challenge to be found, so I fully recommend purchasing The Evil Within 2.

TL;DR - The Evil Within 2 is a vast improvement over its predecessor, placing more focus on building up the atmosphere and environment rather than overemphasis of blood and gore.
---
Gameplay for TEW2 is vastly improved. Gunplay is pretty much the same as the original but the stealth aspect of the game is better now with the cover mechanic. There are different types of weapons for each categories that each serve their different purposes which caters to the different needs of players. i.e. stealthy players may focus more on the silenced pistol to draw enemies one by one, whereas players who prefer straight up combat may go for the more powerful revolver or the more accurate laser-sighted pistol.
Upgrades for weapons and stats for Sebastian are now separated, with weapon parts for upgrading weapons and green gels for upgrading Sebastian and granting him new abilities. In that way, not only can the player build their character according to the playstyle they like, it's is also more difficult to get into the situation whereby the player feels like he/she wasted the materials they used. In addition, green gels actually grants certain useful abilities to Sebastian, such as the ability to strike at unaware enemies from cover, automatically freeing themselves from a grab with a bottle or increased weapon damage with consecutive hits. This is a great departure from the small, minute improvements you get from green gels in the original game.
Crafting is also introduced and seems to draw heavily from Resident Evil 7. This feature gives the player some leeway in using their supplies when venturing through the world, easing them from some on the situations possibly face in the original game whereby they just have not enough bullets to take any boss down. Yet at the same time to prevent this from being abused, the great idea of increased cost when not crafting at a crafting table is greatly increased to deter the wasting of materials unless absolutely desperate for them. I thought this is a really good idea.
Instead of the mostly linear path like the original, TEW2 is now set in an open-world-ish town with a few sidequests that gives more insight on what the background of this game is about.
Story is still whack depending on how invested you were in the lore of the previous title. Newly-inducted players are more likely to find everything more acceptable while the veterans might find the sudden introduction of the new characters (i.e. the daughter) to be more...abrupt.
The best part of this game is the atmosphere and some of the disturbing monsters that haunt you throughout your exploration of the world. With minute usage of jumpscares, the focus and details on the background, eerie music and sometimes cramped environment keeps the players constantly on guard.
I have only one complain - the length of the game feels a bit too short. For a game of this price, i'd expect the story to run on a bit over 25 hours. Playing through the game trying to find all the extra events nets me a total of 15 hours, although to be fair i did not manage to find anything. I also did not try the new game plus mode or higher difficulties.
Whether you liked the original game or not, TEW2 is sure to be a welcomed addition to your library of games.

Have never felt the need to write a review for a "Video Game" but this time I will.
Yes, I finished the game.  Well, I pretty dam satisfied with this purchase.  I saw all the reviews and vidoes on "Youtube" and thought it looked kinda lame.  Really, if you only play the first handful of missions and give up, you probably will think the game is a little tedeous or anoying and miss out on a great game with a great story.  The game does seem to have some graphics issues that can mess with mission 14 and another mission where you have to jump up to a ladder in a burning room but it can all totally be worked around by lowering the video settings "all the way down" - but then again I used an intel i5 quad core PC with a Nvidia 620 card.  A little advise:  Play with your resolution settings until Amanda Ripley can run in the game without the screen jittering (keep your frame rate up) because it affects many parts of the game if your running a lower end card.  There are some parts of the game where you have to hit the E key to trigger events and if your video settings are high, the game will lag and your keystrokes will be out of synch with the game.  Read the forums and comments that are posted on the internet,  There is a fix for any issue you run into, don't quit playing if you run into issues, figure them out.  Anyways:
The ambience of this game is Absolutely Incredible.  I played Dead Space 2 awhile back and loved it but I'm not sure how to really compare the two games other than that they both have a "Bad things are happening in a Space Ship" theme.  You really feel like you are on a functioning 1980's style space station like you've seen in the Aliens movies.  Very good attention to visual details.  The game does not baby sit you 100% through the game like say "Skyrim" does, you may get a little lost in the station sometimes and for whatever reason, I enjoyed looking at the maps and trying to navigate my way around this huge game.  There are areas of the station that are just there for exploring but made the station seem very realistic on a human scale (bathrooms, lounges, maintenance shops, buisinesses, etc).
Some players didn't like the AI characters in the game but I felt that the emotions and actions displayed by the characters were very fitting.  The Alien instincts are realistic and fairly thought out by the designers.  This is not a game where you are playing as a Spec Ops soldier.  You are a young woman that can handle here own, not a highly trained weapons specialist, so don't treat her like one.  You will only be able to stun and scare the alien so don't think you can just go in and kill it either.  Watch the first couple Alien(s) movies, play this game, I'm sure you'll like the game if you liked the movies.  I'm a picky, hard to please 40 year old gamer and I recommend this game - I don't know what else to say without blurting out spoilers.  Play it.

So this game, man this game...was the right step as far as it goes when it comes to Activision producing the same game EVERY YEAR. Every COD up to this point was pretty much the same, within a 5% to 10% margin. This game, not including gunplay, is at least 40% different from other CODs, but I'll explain further.
Single player is pretty much your run-of-the-mill COD experience, from explosions and cliffhangers (literally) to hallway shooting and QTEs. Not much different there other than the exosuit.
And well, the exosuit is pretty much the selling point of this game. It gives the franchise the VERTICALITY that it was always missing, because it's always been a horizontal shooter. Now you can jump, dodge, boost, and now recently, GRAPPLE, through things. And it provides for a different feeling game. If you've played Quake, or jumpy-styled shooters, then this should make you feel a little at home. Although it doesn't feel the same as games like Quake, you will definitely have the edge if you were good at that genre of shooters.
Multiplayer is pretty much all you will play with this game, unless you like Survival and Zombies. It's got your normal COD overlays and uses the pick 10 system from Black Ops 2, but makes it "Pick 13" to account for the Exo-suit abilities. And while the ONLY DOWNSIDE to the game is the LASER NOOBS that ruin multiplayer (#FIXTHELASER), YOU WILL HAVE A GREAT TIME playing this game, whenever you can get into a game.
All in all, this is a very SOLID COD, and for once, Call of Duty did something different for a change...whereas Battlefield made a "DLC" game (Battlefield Hardline). So do I think this game is worth 60 bucks? No. Not for multiplayer alone. If you can get it for less than $50, DO IT. You will have a blast. If jumpy-shooters aren't your thing, Black Ops 2 was the BEST of CODs horizontal shooters.

While most of the art and music design was well done, I really wasn't all that impressed with this game.
-The story was simple and wasn't really anything new, which I understand to be the point, but that resulted in me not being particularly engaged or concerned about anything going on.
-As stated in the description, the battle system does not feature an "attack" button, you only need to press anything for skills. Personally, I dislike this. It makes me feel as though what I'm doing is inevitable, like I have no bearing on what's happening. It was also a tad disorienting at first since the "touching enemies is bad" instinct was active. I suppose the display of damage dealt and the sword animation does make it better than, say, Hydlide, but it's still annoying. Also, perhaps it was just for me, but when it came to crystals or statues that needed to be broken to make a boss vulnerable, I'd have to press "Z", making the system inconsistent.
-Speaking of bosses, the immobile sprites are really unfortunate. Even if they just changed their expression or stance as they were damaged, fighting them could have been much more interesting. The hitboxes are also small for them, as they can only be hit when you're standing directly in front of them. Most attacks done on them knock you back, which can be obnoxious on it's own, but this can also force you into an attack from behind.
-The enemy sprites looked to be stock, or at least designed seperately from Senia's and Magaleta's, because they don't really fit in with the artstyle those two share (taller with colored lineart).
-The translation in the English version is really off. There was one screen near the start where it wasn't even translated at all. I understand that English most likely was not the creator's first language, and the errors can be glanced over if you try, but it still comes off as a lack of effort.
Overall, it's definitely not the worst thing I've played, but I just couldn't enjoy it that much. It's a nice little timewaster, but not something I reccomend or plan on playing again.
TLDR; 5/10: Not my cup of tea, could've been worse.

Eternal Senia takes you back to the time when Aveyond and Cute Knight were the ARPG and 'Girly' games back in the early 2000s. You have NOTHING to lose playing this game as the developer has kindly made it free for everyone on steam! Fighting mechanics are very simple and easy. It didn't really have a strong impact and it's kind of straight forward without much immerson. You go to save your sister and fight through all the crap in the world to try and save her with a few flashbacks thrown in. I didn't feel very drawn into the story, I liked the fighting and art. If anything I would say that that is something that could turn people off, but I didn't dislike it either. If there was anything to improve on in follow up games for the developer, that would be the spot to improve on. Adventure is fun, exploring different terrains, see different beautiful sights, getting different kinds of slimes.

I actually have to go through quite a number of in-game days to make sure the food supply to these slimes are enough for my long adventure. You have to work like a farmer for planting the fruit/veggie and getting the fruit/veggie by yourself. If the fruit/veggie is ripe and left untouched on the ground for too long, it will disappear. Automation of farming will be deeply appreciated,
I love this game, love the idea, love the cuteness of the slimes, but I cannot appreciate the gameplay.

BLACK MESA - HALF LIFE: 2016 EDITION
So, Black Mesa. A project to remake the entirety of Half-Life in the Source engine, with overhauled graphics, sound effects, models, physics, and just about everything. Is it good? Yes. Should you buy it? Probably. Why? Read on.
Although the visuals, sound, and physics have been drastically upgraded, the gameplay has remained the same. Yep, it's still Half-Life, nothing has changed gameplay-wise. You're still Gordon Freeman, you're still in Black Mesa and you're still shooting the s**t out of soldiers and Xenians. It doesn't matter that the gameplay hasn't changed, though: Half-Life's mix of first person shooting and puzzle-platforming was already perfect.
The game looks STUNNING. Seriously, they've really worked magic with the definitely-not-new Source engine. Textures, lighting, colours: all spot on. It really does a lot to bring the environment to life. In the original Half-Life, you'd walk into a room and think "This is a generic room" whereas here you think "This is clearly an employee lounge, look at the decorations and the furniture and the people."
The sound is another area where the devs have outdone themselves, to the point where enemies I wasn't even remotely scared by in HL I am now terrified of. The new zombie sound effects, the rattling breath, the agonized moans and muffled cries for help, the animal-like panting and howling, means that they are pant-wettingly creepy now.
Conclusion: Buy Black Mesa. It may lack the Xen chapters of the game (coming summer 2017) but IMO they were the weakest part of Half-Life and it's not a huge loss. For those who really need Xen then this might not be for you, but even as it stands right now, Black Mesa is an incredible game for those wanting some good ol' Half-Life goodness but not wanting to deal with 1998 levels of physics and graphics.
Feels so good to play that.

That and they've done a spectacular job in recreating and improving upon the original Half-Life.

System Shock 2's legacy lives on partly with the existence of the Deus Ex and Bioshock franchises, but it is more than capable to stand on its own right even today. Despite its outdated controls, GUI and graphics, it trumps most modern titles in terms of atmosphere, immersion, gameplay and story. In fact, many of SS2's features have been integrated into modern games, most notably the presence of audio logs put in unlikely places.
I would recommend taking your time with setting up the game. The standard controls are not good. You will most likely have to rebind your keys based on which weapons/items you choose to use throughout the game, there are so many that you won't get the chance to use them all effectively. The greatest issue I had with this game is that it uses an outdated control scheme for accessing your items. A row of quick access slots, like the one featured in the Deus Ex games, would've been much better for weapon/item access.
Some of the map designs are confusing, and it can be easy to get lost in your first playthrough. Even worse, the game has a minimap function that is disabled by default. Make sure to enable it as soon as you can, it'll make your life much easier.
Resources are scarce. You will be punished for wasting them. On the other hand, the game rewards you for exploration and careful observation. Many items will be placed out of reach or carefully hidden, take your time to find them as long as you aren't under fire.
This game rewards carefulness over gung-ho, reckless charging into unknown areas. Play carefully, lean over corners, use stealth.
You will most likely get frustrated at one point or another for the reasons above and many others, but trust me, this game is worth going all the way to the end. There aren't many games that can offer the experience that System Shock 2 provides nowadays.
The more I think about it, the more I realize that BioShock is just a reskinned version of System Shock 2.

The inspirations from OFF are unmistakeable, the somewhat scribbly artstyle, unsettling music, corporate themes and the tone of oddity and deppression, even Batter and Mortis are in it, and that fact made me a bit worried about this game's subtlety.
While it's a solid RPG with good amount of secrets, several hours playthrough, and an interesting atmosphere mixed with criticism of nearly any political subject (while being dirt cheap of course); it fails with its subtlety when taking on any issues or humorous references.
It took me back to the time when I played OFF or Home, scratches me behind the ears with its familiar eeriness, just to straight up smack me in the face with a wooden plank when trying to jab at some society's issues not tackled by OFF previously.
References are not overwhelming in numbers but astoundingly obvious, its humour is way too often the "meme" type of funny, and relies on making fun of actual internet/political personas, it's all incredibly not universal and very much "here and now", making it feel more shallow than it normally would.
I'm not expecting really high level philosophical stuff from it, and I actually feel relief and joy that its tone wasn't the infamous "capitalism is bad, all for people, it will work cause I say so", but actually critically presented the aspects of it through the medium of its dystopian world.
I'd say that I didn't wish for it to be something more, I wished for it to be something a bit less- to give away its cards with bigger hesitation, have less references to grant its world more substance and soul, something that will make me remember it for longer thanks to its intrigue.
With all that said- it was really fun to play it all the way through, I'd say it's probably worth more than that one dollar, and it doesn't come off as a half a*sed RPG maker game in both art and mechanics.
So the buy is very much recommended (and playing its free inspiration OFF [if you haven't and this is your style]), even if it hadn't any trading cards- it's really worth it.

The art is pretty rough, but it's unique, at least. Anyone that avoids using RPG Maker's default assets deserves some credit. Soundtrack is wacky but enjoyable. Story is... something...

Take this review from someone who played on Nightmare difficulty and really enjoyed the first game.
Pros:
+More personal story
+Better characterization
+Improved graphics (it has gorgeous shadows and lighting effects)
+Combat is still as satisfying
+Lengthy story
+Improved stealth mechanics
+There are wide-open levels
+The wide-open levels have some surprises that tie into the story, so be sure to explore
+Cool bosses
+Runs pretty well on my old FX-6350 CPU and GTX 970 GPU. (Mostly ultra settings at 40-50 FPS)
+Has genuinely terrifying set pieces
Note how I say wide-open levels because this is not an open-world game. There are just levels that are surprisingly expansive.
Cons:
-Voice acting is a bit wooden at times
-Different voice actors (but they do grow on you)
-Sebastian is still a bit awkward to control especially with the new cover system
-Some of the dialogue is awkward
-Villains could be more developed
-Bosses aren't as memorable compared to the first game's bosses
-Side missions aren't very interesting
-Enemy AI is dumb and completely exploitable
-Stealth kill upgrades make the game too easy
Overall, this is a great game if you love Japanese horror, or just horror in general. It's a big improvement on the first game in terms of optimization, story, gameplay, and graphics. Although stealth killing makes many parts of the game easy, there is still challenge to be found, so I fully recommend purchasing The Evil Within 2.
