That's your tl;dr. It sums up the game, to be honest. The Evil Within 2 is indeed fun in certain parts, don't get me wrong, but the game isn't scary. It has one or two good moments for someone not used to horror games and...that's about it.
Here are the pros: combat is sort of fun, level design is pretty good, game has good visuals and even some creatively designed monsters. Shooting enemies is fun, and being able to give your character skills is good. And that's about it.
The Evil Within 2 markets itself as an open world rpg horror game with shooter elements. Don't be fooled, though; the open world areas are fairly small and there are very linear sections. It might be more accurate to call the game a 'game that calls itself open world which really means you can explore a bit if you want'. There's not really that much exploration and the side quests don't really matter to the overall plot. A truly open world horror game would have been great, but I guess the developers couldn't make that work.
The monsters in the game are slightly challenging before you learn the mechanics, and then almost laughably easy. I played on the Normal difficulty and I could have done Nightmare pretty easily. None of the boss fights were even close to intense; I died in only one of the fights and generally only died while playing if I forgot to heal up.
Are all these flaws unforgivable? No, they wouldn't drag down a game with great storytelling or amazing scares. Too bad The Evil Within 2 has neither. I got scared at the start because I thought the game would be scarier than it was. But it never suprised me or made me feel uncomfortable. Clearly one of the villains is meant to be a horrific monster who pushes the boundaries of what we consider normal...he's almost laughably silly. For a horror game, the greatest sin it can commit is being boring and predictable, and that's the biggest flaw this game has right now: the story sucks.
The villains are not scary or captivating, and the side characters are as interesting as a plastic bag. Not that the first game had an amazing villain either; he was cliched as well. But at least you had two side characters, Kidman and Joseph who had a tiny bit of personality you could care about. In this game, all the side characters are like sticks you occasionally interact with.
And then there's our main character, good old Sebastian Castellanos. He's...the most cliche of stereotypes. He's the suffering detective, the bitter alcoholic seeking redemption, the desperate father who lost his daughter and has to get her back. Nothing about him will suprise you, and it's depressing how unoriginal Tango Gameworks made this character.
Honestly, it annoyed me how much I stopped liking this game. I'm not a horror fan, but I liked watching people play the first game on Youtube enough to play it myself. And it had some fun moments. But this game...no. There's a ton of positive reviews for it, but I don't see how people can call this game intriguing or provocative unless they truly are newcomers to horror games. The Evil Within 2 has the most reused plot lines, the lamest villains, and the most cardboard protagonist I've seen in a while. Some of the monsters look cool, but that's it.
The game developers should be ashamed of themselves for creating something so forgettable. This game is definitely not worth your $60, and maybe not $30 either. If you want to be entertained and you don't mind wading through some boring scenes, I'd still recommend you try this out. For $10, maybe. But if you're looking for a scary game, a fun game that will keep you invested in the characters, or a classic game you won't forget, look somewhere else.

I am 11 hours in. I am playing at Hard. I am not the usual person that claims to be invicable towards horror films, I get frightened from Horror films more than once. The problem is....Alien Isolation is marketed as survival horror, but its not scary.
Basically, this game without the horror aspect makes it a pale shadow of its potential. The gameplay is slow, I don't have any complaints against that, the original movie WAS slow after all. The Alien AI is really easy to dodge, and the fact that you can hide from it deletes the potential of some really scary moments. Seriously, the hiding mechanic erases every fear element in the game. I'm not saying that hiding in one place makes you invincible towards the enviroment, but the mechanic saves your bacon more than needed, and takes the  fear out of the game. On the bright side, for some people the mechanic is their cup of tea.
Another problem is its wasted potential. The game could have used some light and dark elements to scare the player, maybe the use of dust in the air to scare the player, a surprise alien jumpscare to shock the player. I know that jumpscares are cheap, but the game is so dull it needs them.
Alien Isolation is more of a stealth game than a horror game. I see so much reviews for this game, maybe I'm playing it wrong, because I really tried my best to enjoy it, I really did! I tried my best to feel the atmosphere, to try the most stealth apporach, but the game falls flat, a middle child between stealth and horror, and is acknowledged by neither.
DO NOT BUY ALIEN ISOLATION AS A HORROR GAME, BUY IT AS A STEALTH GAME.
TL:DR, only people that are filled with nostalgia over the movie, or stealth enthusiast can enjoy this game. I rue the day I chose to buy this game over Shadow Of Mordor, even though Shadow Of Mordor also looks bland, it does in fact look in the least enjoyable.

First- a note to the devs: GIVE US A WAY TO SKIP DIALOG AND CUTSCENES!
Now, with that out of the way.
This game has been on my wishlist for a while now. The recent change that allowed us to download the first chapter was a welcome one. I'm sick of how many games have gone to an episodic format but I'm much less turned off when I can try the game first, even if I'm fairly sure I'm going to like the game.
And I'm old. I played all the original Sierra game many years ago. I don't remember much of anything about it but I'm sentimental about the series regardless.
And with even more of that crap out of the way let me get to reviewing what I've played so far...
It's great. It's fun. And I've enjoyed the hell out of playing most of the first chapter. I think a standout so far is the voice acting and actors. So many adventure games have horrible dialog and actors and happily this one doesn't kill my soul with banality or downright lack of talent. The voice cast here fits well and for the most part kicks butt. Not to mention the  total fan-service with little hidden gems- (and here I'll take a little parenthetical diversion- Little touches like Christopher Lloyd giving us a tiny dialog easter egg after the Battle of Wits. Or freaking Wallace "Vizzini" Shawn from Princess Bride doing an openly and awesomly great homage to the aforementioned movie.)
There are puns. And those of us who happen to love fantasy writers like Piers Anthony are fine with that. More than fine with actually. And we groan lovingly at them. As we should.
The controls can be wonky at times but are serviceable enough. The quicktime events are only slightly annoying (until right after the battle of wits) unlike most games that rely on them to create a complete teeth gnashingly pointless challenge that makes you want to smash every keyboard in your house.
The game looks good. It's very "Telltale" in its execution but I'm fine with that. It works and it works well.
Overall I was likely to buy the game regardless of whether they made the first chapter free- I would have just waited for a sale after the whole series was released. And I may wait until it comes down in price just a little bit. But I'm buying the whole game as soon as I can't stand waiting anymore.
So for once the episodic model has worked (and a note to future game developers STOP MAKING EPISODIC GAMES. IT'S A STUPID RELEASE FORMAT AND MAKES US HATE YOU TO YOUR VERY CORE- just give us the beginning of the game as a demo and we'll follow like lemmings).
And a side note to the jerks who complain about a game being too easy. Screw you. Stop insisting that every game punishes you. Did your mother not give you enough hugs and make you perform impossible tasks in order to get attention? Some of us like to play games for pure entertainment value. And this one does this impossibly well.
I hope Sierra tries to relive some more of the old magic they used to give us all those years ago.

Moderately fun, but far too frustrating to play vs the older Total War games.  In the end it made me break out the original Rome Total War and load that up.
The good:
- The new way of managing regions by using sub-regions is interesting.
- The new army system is interesting, and the stance system makes more sense then trying to find the right forest to hide your army in.
- The port seige and mixed army/navy battles
- AI does a much better job of trying to counter moves intelligently in battle.
- graphics are awesome
The bad:
- The army system means that you can no longer have a small sub-army controlled by a captain cover a separate path, or travel by itself between regions.
- The controls are frustrating to learn
- Units didn't seem to always obey the commands I gave, even before battle was joined.
- New system means that cities now have to specialize in something
- Have to reinforce/build troops directly at the army
- No control over what types of garrison forces are placed in cities.
- I had to have graphics turned down to medium on my R9 270 in order to get an average of 22fps, so it didn't really look any better graphically than Shogun II.
Total:
I would give this only a 5.5-6 out of 10, whereas I give most of the other Total War games 7-9's.

Clandestine, a two-player co-op game that's unique in the sense of how it plays where one of the players takes the role of a spy, that plays in the third person view, where you have to complete the objectives presented to you like stealing data, or killing a whole bunch of people..etc, without getting spotted or killed. The other player takes the role of a hacker that's behind the scenes, away from the action, providing intel for the spy player like spotting enemies and cameras, where you can disable and/or use for your advantage, and hacking a door systems to get the code to give to the spy for him/her to open the locked door, and more like sounding alarms for distractions..etc. Also it's worth to mention that you can play this solo, hoping from the hacker to the spy and vice versa. The game is a hard stealth game by the way, as in like one or two shots and you're dead.
The game also has, for the spy, two types of clothing/armor where one of them would be spy gear with more protection and whatnot, but you would be instantly suspected and spot if seen wearing it, while the other choice is wearing normal civilian cloth which decreases your spy abilities in some ways, but removes all suspension in certain levels when seen, unless you go to restricted areas, go on and kill some one..you know, the thing that one does to receive suspicion, and that's kind of a nice touch.
To me this is a great idea, combining two different gameplay types in a coop like mode, and haven't seen a game do this kind of thing before ( at least for me ) and it has my support and recommendation as a great game with great innovative potential, but it needs a lot of refinement / improvements in terms of how the game controls on both sides of the game ( the spy and the hacker ) with how the gameplay feeling really clunky seeing as how it's on Steam Early Access as version 0.1. And i hope they improve the tutorial as the hacker, also improving how you hack seeing as it's time consuming and annoying to hack something and then moving to hack something else, a click and drag system would be better, and if you're wondering what i mean by this is as a hack you have sort of a squid icon and you have to move it with you're arrow keys in certain lines, which becomes a pain really fast when using it.
The game is in development and i want to play more of it once it has been polished, and will get back to it on another new post in the future once the improvements are in place, and i want it to improve because i like the idea behind it and the fun coop gameplay that comes with it, and so if you want to support the idea, help developing it by getting it and providing feedback, wanting to see this game shine, then I'm with you, it also has a handful of levels to play with if you're wondering, but if you're thinking that it 'looks cool' and don't want to deal with how a game is in development with it's bugs and un-refinements, then i suggest you wait.

Initially, I was hesitant to buy this game because of the price and lack of catalogue behind this developer. However, putting some faith into this game I took a risk and bought it straight-out. It was the right choice... kind of.
This is a third person stealth game with a female lead, which is rare nowadays given the genre. However, that isn't why this game has potential, it's the old school "PS2" feeling Clandestine holds that held me all the way through. If you didn't play many PS2 games, don't worry, you can get to experience a modern outlook of what stealth gameplay use to be like. The game is fun if but flawed but then again this is the first releasse of an alpha and there is plenty of room for improvement.
There are nice touches here and there, but also problems here and there. The character model, certain animations, gameplay mechanics (like the hacking) I can tell have work put into them but this game needs more money and polish put into it for it to really exceed. The problems being janky controls to it, no, not the tank control your character has, but actions like calling an elevator, using the cover system, feels.... off, not fluid enough. There's also the lack of any graphical options, shadows, atmosphere, any decent music, hell, voice acting. The shooting is quite bland, the NPC models are generic and the UI could do with a less clean look, in my opinon.
So why am I recommending this game then? Because it has the promise, and potential, to be amazing. Also I want to see more games like this instead of the cluster♥♥♥♥ of cloned 2D games we're all seeing now, this game feels like a breath of fresh air and to its credit, it did keep me entertained. All this needs is more man hours put into it!
Oh yeah, this has co-op functionality, so there's that.

The first Dishonored is my favorite game of all time. Obviously, I was anxious for the day to come where I could reprise my role as Royal Protector Corvo Attano, or I could possess the role of Empress Emily Kaldwin, who has a slew of new abilities. As of now, I am around 10 hours into my playthrough as Emily and I must say that this is exactly what I expected from this sequel. Of course, there are multiple ways of reaching your target and also multiple ways to take down your target. Each power now has a more in-depth upgrade tree in which you can allow Corvo's Blink to be redirective, as Daud's was in the Knife of Dunwall and the Brigmore Witches, or you can upgrade Emily's Doppleganger ability to create copies of yourself that will fight for you.
A new feature that I was very excited for was Bonecharm Crafting. This works by sacrificing a bone charm's trait so that you will be able to create a single bone charm with multiple traits taken from a sacrificed charm. You can create a single charm with two, three, or four traits, however, corrupted charms have made a reappearance from Daud's DLC. The more traits you add onto a crafted bone charm, the more likely it will be come corrupted and apply a negative attribute along with the traits you applied to it.
I don't know much about graphics, but I can tell you that this game's graphics are outstanding. I will occasionally stop and stare at the scenery, which will sometimes appear as a beautiful painting. The art style has remained the same and it helps with its look that much more.
There are new enemies, such as the Nest Keepers and the Clockwork Soldiers that will help gameplay from feeling repetitive. There are new faces, as well as old ones. There are new powers that can be heavily upgraded (if you can find the resources to do so), and old ones with new attributes to be added onto them. There's an entirely new system for bone charms that can be ignored if you do not care for corrupted charms. There are new places to explore, and there are old, but familiar ones that make this sequel feel that much more like Dishonored.
This game has gotten a lot of criticism for its performance, but looking past this inconvenience, Dishonored 2 is yet another masterpiece created by the masterminds at Arkane Studios. In my opinion, Dishonored 2 is hands-down my Game of the Year and I would recommend this piece of art to each and every one of you.

MY REVIEW FOCUSES ON THE STORY AND STEALTH GAMEPLAY. Therefore, it is the CENTER OF MY CRITISISM, whilst other areas are good or better described by others.
*STORY*
In my view, the core of any game, especialyl if it has or at least tries to establish a solid character arc is the story. I was not touched by the opening scene simply because I had no connection to Lilly or Myra whatsoever. Lilly is cute and Myra is my beloved wife but I don't care - they must mean something to me, and the fact that they are my family is not enough. It is way to cliche. I have to value them and to be affraid of their loss.
The lack of intriguing plot makes it very hard to carry on simpy because I get bored. Top that with the need to upgrade Sebastien, since I am playing on the nightmare difficulty and just in case if you don't go for additional ammo, power buffs and better equipment - you'll get bent over.
This process greatly increases the gap between the main storyline and that is where all passion fades away. I don't feel like keep going, although it is a solid game. It is just boring and if I can predict all the story twists and curves the intrigue fades away, being subbed by "oh boy, I saw it coming, just like in the ...." or "well, now it will be either this or that... here it goes! I called it!"
That may not be the case for you, if this game is one of your first horror experiences or games in general, but that issue dissolved any interest for me to carry on.
*EDIT*
***I loved the scene where Myra tells you that it was not your fault for losing Lilly. With music accompaniment, that moment was really powerful and made me smile. But gues what? It happens on the 12th hour of gameplay. This is not good enough and bad storytelling ruins all the hard work completed by other departments.***
*STEALTH*
Due to the described difficulties, going stealth is a great gateway. That will save you a lot of ammo and medkits. However, cover system is a bit buggy which will result in Sebastien getting stuck or stoping in between changing cover, thus being exposed to his enemies.
What's more is that sometimes a take down from behind won't work, which means you'll need to run away, hide, wait it out and then repeat... Does not happen evey time, but when it does - it is annoying.
Therefore, the best conclusion from that issue is not that the stealth sucks, but that it should be used to avoid your enemies. Take this advice and it will save you time, ammo, medkits and nerves. Remember - stealth is not the best way of neutralizing your enemies but for avoiding them. A negative turned into a positive))).
So, this is my conclusion - if  the story does not concern you, if the character arc is not the vital component - you will enjoy this game. There are so many positive reviews which claim the story to be great and I think that this view should be balanced out. In any case - you are the judge and your opinion is yours only.

I am 11 hours in. I am playing at Hard. I am not the usual person that claims to be invicable towards horror films, I get frightened from Horror films more than once. The problem is....Alien Isolation is marketed as survival horror, but its not scary.
Basically, this game without the horror aspect makes it a pale shadow of its potential. The gameplay is slow, I don't have any complaints against that, the original movie WAS slow after all. The Alien AI is really easy to dodge, and the fact that you can hide from it deletes the potential of some really scary moments. Seriously, the hiding mechanic erases every fear element in the game. I'm not saying that hiding in one place makes you invincible towards the enviroment, but the mechanic saves your bacon more than needed, and takes the  fear out of the game. On the bright side, for some people the mechanic is their cup of tea.
Another problem is its wasted potential. The game could have used some light and dark elements to scare the player, maybe the use of dust in the air to scare the player, a surprise alien jumpscare to shock the player. I know that jumpscares are cheap, but the game is so dull it needs them.
Alien Isolation is more of a stealth game than a horror game. I see so much reviews for this game, maybe I'm playing it wrong, because I really tried my best to enjoy it, I really did! I tried my best to feel the atmosphere, to try the most stealth apporach, but the game falls flat, a middle child between stealth and horror, and is acknowledged by neither.
DO NOT BUY ALIEN ISOLATION AS A HORROR GAME, BUY IT AS A STEALTH GAME.
TL:DR, only people that are filled with nostalgia over the movie, or stealth enthusiast can enjoy this game. I rue the day I chose to buy this game over Shadow Of Mordor, even though Shadow Of Mordor also looks bland, it does in fact look in the least enjoyable.

Eternal Senia is an a RPG Maker game. Before I continue this review, I best get that out of the way, so that those of you who detest the engine and it's games can move on.
Now, having said that it is an RPG Maker game. I must admit, I myself was highly sceptical that this would be any good. But, the screenshots and art style drew me in and so did that ever so kind price tag of: FREE! So, onto the review.
First item on the list, the narrative. Eternal Senia is a romantic tale in as many ways as it is a drama. It's a tale of the length and extent one human will go to, to save the person whom they love. It's a tale about the psychological pressure's one will experience metaphorically whilst fighting for the place in the rightful eyes of those whom they hold dear. In essence what I'm trying to say is that, the tale, whilst short and fairly simplistic. Is a good one. It kept me hooked for the duration of the game and it made me intrigued enough to continue pushing on through to find out what happens in the end. Yet the end, is a fascinating feels trip, and (depending on which ending you get) may not satisfy what you wanted all along and make you question the outcome. Something in my personal opinion, any good RPG should be aiming for. To get the player to ponder and question the outcome is a good tale indeed.
Now, from the storyline to that of the most important aspect, the combat. The combat for this game is a fairly standard affair for those of you who have played non turn-based RPG Maker games and is in fact much easier than most standard games as this was the developers intention. The battles/boss battles can all be fought and won with strategy and tactics rather than sheer force, for those of you who are less interested in grinding. Having said that, the frequency of save points, the arcane realm (an in-game arena of sorts) and the huge amount of loot drops which can be crafted make the game's grinding seamless and in many cases you will not feel it a chore to level up. I myself managed to make to the level cap by the end of the game without realising as the various collectible "side-quests" you get in each dungeon quickly increase your exp without noticing. So, for completionists, you're in luck as you're partly rewarded with this game. This all goes hand-in-hand with the developers intentions of creating a simple to play story based RPG. It should aslo be noted, that the game also makes use of key-binded "skills" gifted to the player throughout the game. These skills are used for a variety of combat situations and occasional puzzles. These skills can also be upgraded using SP (Skill Points) which are awarded to the player after killing enemies in-game. Also, throughout the game, some enemies will drop pages or even books as a loot. These pages and books can be used to award permanent boosts the player's overall skills. You will also be awarded more of these if you complete the additional "side-quests". That is all that can be said for the combat of the game. Now we move onto:
Length/Replayability. This game as you might have guessed is indeed a short one. Given that it is a free game I'm sure you could not have expected it to be particularly long. The game by itself without gathering the collectibles or killing monster kings should take you no more than 3 hours. If you're a perfectionist collecting every item and completing the "side-quests" should yield a time of 4-5 hours. If you were to present yourself a challenge and attempt the game's bosses on hard mode, you'd find yourself looking at a modest 5-6 hour timespan. As for replayability, the game has 3 ending outcomes. These do not require the game to be replayed and all you need to do is make one save before the final boss (you will be given ample warning of this in-game) and then change your accessories before the fight each time. These accessory combinations will provide the various outcomes for the game. So, there is not much in the way of replayability.
Now for those who skim read, here's a pro/cons list and a TL;DR:
- Interesting Storyline.
- Simplistic, yet fluid combat system.
- Easier combat system for casual players/RPG newcomers.
- Acheivable and short collectible "side-quests"
- Simplistic yet effective character customisation.
- Upgradeble skills.
- 3 Endings.
- Story is slightly cliche in places.
- Short gameplay time.
- Combat can become slightly repetitive.
- Occasional RPG Maker puzzles.
TL;DR: The game is good. it's free, short, and is perfect for a small yet engaging feel train with some solid, albeit repetitive combat mechanics. I would highly recommend it as it is in my personal opinion one of the best RPG Maker games on Steam at this time. I mean, you really have nothing to lose. The game is FREE!

Just Cause 3 is basically just Just Cause 2 but with added improvements including a grapple that can tether more than once and can retract, allowing the player to tear down structures or attach two enemies together. There are a good variety of weapons and vehicles ranging from mortars to nuke launchers and tanks with energy shields, there are plenty to fuel your destruction.
Compared to Just Cause 2, the weapons and vehicles are better (although lack of a Tuk-Tuk Boom is disappointing) and the grapple and wingsuit add new dimensions. As a base game, Just Cause 3 is just Just Cause 2 with a new map and more to play with, unlike how Just Cause 2 was a complete makeover compared to the first Just Cause.
Is it worth full price? I don't think so, although I bought this game off ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for £17 and got a free game as a bonus. For £17 this game is definitely worth it.
The upcoming DLC including Sky Fortress certainly looks fun, I'll make a review for the DLC when each is released.
Overall, if you are expecting a game completely better than Just Cause 2, then this is not it. If you are a person who hasn't played a Just Cause game before, then this is a brilliant game to play. For a price like £39.99 it is not worth it for any interested party, although considering I got it for £17 off from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it is best to get it from there and the price is getting cheaper all the time.

After reading a vast number of like negative reviews--some of which had perfectly justifiable content and concern, I decided to buy this game from another site that sells keys for the whopping price of 20 usd. That was a purchase price I could live with, given the mountainous bad reviews for this title. You know, unlike similar games (GTA and Far Cry for example), the reviews for Just Cause 3 were almost 50/50 right out of the gate. It's still such that only six and a half guys out of any room full of ten would give it a thumbs-up. My skepticism aside, I bought it.
I was hoping that Just Cause 3 was going to be Just Cause 2, only better. When you approach this title with that expectattion in mind, you'll find yourself very pleased. Players jumping into this franchise here may find it a bit chaotic or loosely-knit.
In my opinion, it's a playground for those with A.D.D.
Something is going to distract you or prevent you from reaching seemingly short, relatively- easy tasks. That could be the astounding beauty of a simulated sunflower, the dazzling surround sound offered through a Dolby headset, or just goofing off with your parachite and grappling hook. Yes--those are the core elements of travel here again. Zip, pull, zip, pull, zip, pull!
Everything is drivable, flyable, or aqua-manueverable. You can skydive from the highest heights of swim to the bottom of the seas. Every inch in between is beautifully-rendered in an early matrix-esque representation of a Mediterranean seaside country.
You have innumerable fun experiments to be had using your grappling hooks, tethers, winches, and rocket-propelled explosives. When the tedious grind gets you down, take a stroll into town and tie-up a civilian to a gas canister. Fire a shot into the cylinder to send the attached person flying through the air. Tether a helicopter. Tether the ground. Watch as a tethered helicopter helplessly plummets to the ground in a tight arc, still tethered. Use a hot hatchback as a wrecking ball by tethering it to a helicopter a flying about town smashing statues and propaganda trucks.
This has some of the best elements of some of my favorite video games all wrapped into one neat package.
Reading some of the negative reviews got me to investigating and what I turned-up was that most of those who didn't respond positively to this title were grossly under-equipped with store-bought PCs and little to no video cards.
This isn't DOOM or Sim City. It's not slow or boring by anybody's sense of the words. This is a modern, relatively new title that is designed from the ground up to utilize some of the best parts availble in today's custom PC market. And ladies and gentlemen, when it does that, and you're using adequate rigs top run this, it is the next best thing to GTA.
In any foreseeable future, the only thing I'd like to see from Just Cause 3 is multiplayer. Although it took some years and more fans than it should've, the Just Cause 2 Multiplayer patch was one of the most fun additions to a game I've played in years. When that days comes and they develope a multiplayer, this will be on par with the big boy titles. Until then, it may remain a treasured classic to Tomb Raider and Uncharted fans, but may not give much in the way of replayability in the long-run.
All-in-all, I'd say this game is sure worth the $20 I spent for it. But unless you're getting add-ons or extras, I wouldn't pay more than $30 or so. Wait till this title comes down, and in the meantime, reinvest in your PC. My top two suggestions? A video card or video card upgrade and an appropriately-sized power supply.

Ah man, where do I start with this game. This game is one of the greatest computer games I have ever played. From the creators of Thief, and it’s just as good. Anyway, let’s get into this.
DISCLAIMER: This review will include some forms of spoilers
Gameplay- The gameplay is very nice; very easy to get into. Admittingly the two different forms of HUD were a little funky at first, but I quickly got use to it, and I enjoyed running in one direction away from Hybrids while trying to reload my gun with a different set of bullets. The “Cyber Modules” system was also good. Using Cyber Modules you can upgrade the player’s Stats, Weapons Skills, Psi Powers, and Tech. At the start of the game it’s easy to get into upgrading your character with the different Cyber Modules you are given or pick up throughout the Von Braun, and then as the game goes on Upgrades start costing more and more Cyber Modules to the point where each Cyber Module you receive is like the greatest thing ever, and that my friends, is how you do a Upgrade system. I never actually got into the Psi Powers, so I can’t say much on that, but of what I did it was pretty cool and snazzy.
Graphics- The game was made in 1999 for Computers… So that should say something about the graphics. But the graphics aren’t horrid, they’re easy to look at, but it actually took the “Horror” aspect of the game down a bit because of how laughable some of the enemies look. There are some mods are textures you can download however to increase the quality of the textures, and those do look good so I would recommend them.
Setting- As I mentioned above, the game is “Horror”. However, it is much more than just a Horror game(and as I mentioned before the graphics make it not all that scary). In the first few parts of the game you’ll come across the occasional severed limb or head. But as the game goes on they start appearing less and less until they’re just gone for good almost. In my opinion that shows that the developers weren’t trying to make a full out Horror game (of the Hollywood variety anyway). There are also a couple dead bodies hanging from the ceiling with horrific face expressions, but I only find like three of those. The main enemies in the game are Hybrids, which look like humans with a worm coming out of their chest biting onto their head, but really, it’s not all that scary. Now that I’ve covered the Horror parts of the game, it’s time to talk about how the game isn’t actually a “Horror” game. As I said before there is so much more to the game. It is definitely a Suspense game, and that it does perfectly. The game depends on the mysteries and suspense to creep you out rather than gore, which is great for the game. There are also the many Audio-logs left by the dead crew members. Many of these Logs help flesh out the history of the ship and it’s inhabitants, and all that happens before the start of the game. Some of the Logs you’ll wish you never read… Ehehehehe
*Spoilerriffic stuffs start here*
SHODAN is also a very important point of the game. Starting from her reveal up to the end of the game the game is at it’s best, with her constantly talking to you and prodding you along in her distorted yet adorable(I kid) voice. SHODAN’s interactions with the player are some of the best parts of the game: “I AM SHODAN”, “I-I-Insect!”, “Can’t you do anything right?!”
I was actually pretty disappointed when she betrayed me, I thought me and her had something, D:
*End*
VERDICT- This game is great, but probably not for everyone. If you are a fan of darker games or just want to play a game that’ll scare you(DARN ROBOTS!) but not give you nightmares, play this. Also I recommend this to fans of the “Thief” series, as it is made by the same studio and shares many voices(Stephen Russel, FTW!). This game took “Sci-Fi Horror” and made something great. I would really like to see a third game someday… *looks off into the sunset*
Anyway, 8.5/10! It’s a great game!
ALSO: I highly recommend listening to Cryoshell’s Breakout while playing the game!

This is the first time I've felt moved to review a game on Steam.  I'm a huge gamer - and I especially love old PC games, challenging games, obtuse games.  But I just can't quite dig System Shock 2.  I tried a playthough doing the PSI route, and it was so insanely hard that I thought I was missing something, or not understanding the rules of the game.  I tried again going the Military route, which was much better, but after a few hours of gameplay I think I've had enough.
I love challenging gameplay - I'm a decent gamer.  But there are design issues as far as I'm concerned.  You can save/load anytime you like - but the game is so brutally unforgiving (there are many times you literally can't do anything about just constantly losing health, from radioation or toxins, etc) that it becomes a "save, load, save, load" kind of experience.  You can use anti-toxin hypos, but because of the design, its almost better just to reload and try again, because hypos are so ridiculusly rare.  There are places you can regenerate in the game, which seem redundant with the save/load always available.  I invest in maintenence, but there are no repair tools.... like, for HOURS of gameplay.  I invest in repair, but I'm not even sure how I'm supposed to repair things.  I invest in energy weapons, but after so many saves and loads I seem to have left an energy weapon somewhere, so that's out, as I won't see another one for another hour probably.  It's one nonstop annoyance after another, this game, as far as gameplay mechanics.
The atmosphere is great, sure.... the story and audio logs are amazing.  I can't think of any other game I was more excited to actually listen to the audio logs you find throughout the world.  The creepy factor is superb. I love the arcade, old-school style challenge.  But the whole ability to save/load at any time sort of undermines the experience.... it's almost just as good to use your wrench and just keep doing save/loads until you get lucky and get through a series of hallways.  I invested in research, and the chemicals I needed were in a DIFFERENT chemical storage room, far away.  Really?  How many dang chemicals are in this game?  Sheesh.  Is it worth it?
It seems to suffer from nerds-designing-games.  It's incessantly complex, but it feels arbitrary.
I'm genuinely confused at the good press and reviews.  I think I actually hate this game on a gameplay level.  I think only if you designed it, you would know how to play it.
This is just my opinion - but I've played games for decades, I'm a fan of tough games from Another World to Dark Souls, Doom to VVVVVV.  But this just feels kind of sloppy and "save, die, load, save, die, load, save, die."
I'm sure people will say, you don't know how to play it, or something.... but I actually feel like I don't.  I tried a few times... it went better the second playthrough, but.... I think I'm over it..... just my opinion.

A very addictive, and surprisingly enjoyable game about cramming slimes in pens and selling their poop.
I am looking forward to future content updates, but I will go into a few suggestions that may or may not make be addressed later.
1. Add a breeding option with the slimes. Right now you can create a hybrid of two slimes, making a largo version with a combination of both traits. This is still interesting and useful, but I feel some complexity could be added by allowing a way to "create" new slimes, even if it was just a fancy machine that took two slimes and makes a third if it was one of the preselected pairings.
2. Automation. I read that this is part of a future content patch, but this was the biggest concern for me. I wanted to explore, but I felt like I had to spend a great deal of my time picking up crops, feeding slimes, and selling plorts. Automating this doesn't have to mean removing these steps, but apart from the plort collector, many of the upgrades don't make the individual tasks easier.
3. More complexity in the market. Right now it seems if you sell plorts on one day, it will go down in price the next. Sell more the next day and it will drop further until it hits a baseline value. If you ignore a market, the prices go back up. This makes sense if the goal is to force diverse ranching to keep up profits. Instead, the "best" option I saw is to stockpile plorts of a given type until the market is high, sell them all, then ignore the market until it maxes out again. A market that fluctuates more outside of your control, or is more resiliant to just a few sales might make for a better system.
4. Faster energy regeneration. Too often I am trying to explore new areas and I just have to sit around for a few seconds while my energy regen kicks in. Maybe make it start earlier if there are no slimes or dangers around.

Cute but shallow; the gameplay in its current state is virtually identical to the way it was at early access launch, though now it features a few (one or two?) more shallow, linear areas and a couple more slimes.
The game consists entirely of sucking up slimes, sticking them in a pen, feeding them their favored food (fruit, vegetables, or meat), and then selling their plorts. You use the money from selling their plorts to buy more pens to hold more slimes, or more areas to hold more pens to hold more slimes, and though they all behave a little bit differently, and look different, it's effectively the same exact thing every time you do it.
You can also grow the food for your slimes, but it consists of simply sticking chickens in a pen, where they automatically multiply, or a fruit into a field, where it immediately grows into a tree and spawns fruit every day.
The game very quickly becomes tedious, as none of this can be automated, so once you've gotten all your slimes penned (takes less than 30 minutes) and your food planted/penned, you could theoretically just sleep every day away, go gather all your slime food, stick it in the pen autofeeder, sell the plorts, and then sleep again. There's nothing pushing you to do more than that, and nothing to see even if you do. All the areas in the game are just big empty linear pathways where slimes hop around eating whatever they can fit into their mouths, waiting to be sucked up and stuck in a pen by you. Sometimes they turn into weird goo monsters and kill all the other slimes until they themselves die, and then more slimes just pop out of the ground, so none of it matters.
It's kind of a bummer, but whatever, it's not like there isn't Stardew Valley, Rune Factory, Story of Seasons, and two decades of Harvest Moon games to play instead. Hell, even that garbage heap Innocent Life is a better game than this.

So a couple of days ago I got this game with the current discount that Steam offers (33% off) I thought frankly the game wasn't only incredibly badly optimized, but also it was a boring and dull experience, I didn't experience crashes or anything of the sort, but I did experience framedrops on the second mission during the infamous intro sequence as well as when staring down towards the city from the balcony.
I tried every setting imaginable and I just couldn't get a playable framerate, I tried everything I could, but for my standars, (which are high because I guess i'm a jerk) the game was just unplayable, it drop to the low 40 fps with some settings set to the lowest that they could get, in other cases the game just simply refused to stay above 30 fps, and so on and so forth, after having a confusing, and frustrating experience, I pretty much just refunded the game, that was of course until today.
I found a deal for the game at a "legit" website (according to a Bethesda representative that hangs around some forums on reddit) and whooptie doo, here we have my review. And I managed to fix my performance issues, How?
Welp...
i5 6600k
gtx 970
24 gb of ram
Those up there are my system specs, not to shabby, not to incredible, in my honest opinion, just a decent enough build.
I first disabled vsync completely, it turns out the input lag as well as the fact that it's the type of vsync that imposes double buffering, an uncommon form of applying vsync now a days, usually games use triple buffering without even telling you, to my understanding the simple rule of this to forms of vsync goes like this, double buffered locks your framerate at the half of your monitor's refresh rate, so if my monitor has an hz of 60, the game will simply lock my framerate to 30.
Triple buffering fixes this, but sadly it introduces an absurd amount of input lag, so the only solution for this was to disable vsync completely, something that both fixed in it's entirety the issue with the input lag, as well as the framerate issue, for the most part.
The second thing that I did was to set the game at the "default settings" meaning to have the game running at the recommended settings that the game offers based on my system specs.
It appears it set everything to the "medium" preset, the game looks good, nothing spectacular, nothing ugly, just good.
And... That's pretty much it, the game now runs and plays just fine, I just finished the first two levels and I felt the need to give a write up for this, maybe I experience problems at a later date, I hope not, but there.
DIshonored 2 as a game, when talking about the core, of the story, of the gameplay, of the actual experience, it's an absolute masterpiece so far, and i've put in maybe around two hours or so, with the first one being the one that made me slap my head and refund the game, and with the second one being one fueled by my curiosity as well as by my care for my limited income.
And i'm glad in all honesty that I purchased the game again, I really enjoy it, but that's not to say the game doesn't have it's fare share of problems, the game is plaguated by performance issues across all systems, for what i'm reading.
Maybe I could recommend it for people that don't mind dropping the settings down a bit, nor do other people that maybe don't mind playing the game at 30fps just like the rest of the platforms do, overall tho, I really hope they fix this on pc, because what i'm experiencing now, after a lot of trial an error, and just a lot of pacience and tolerance, is not what the regular buyer needs nor will it do, in most cases people will simply forget about the game and move along, and for a game that was clearly made with this much passion, with as much attention to detail, and with as much care, I frankly don't think it's fair, not to the consumer, and not to the creators themselves, to have them releasing this much of a broken mess.
Even then, i'm recommending it, because in my experience, is a great game, incredible really... If you can get it to play.

OK, this review will be a difficult one... Let's start with the first half of the game. First two (tutorial) hours were kinda meh, but after I got to the third chapter, I was instantly hooked on and started having a lot of fun. Scavenging semi-openworld locations are great, action is well balanced and fun, there are a lot of great mindf*ck moments, world in STEM makes a lot more sense than in first TEW and villain is also very interesting and I couldn't wait what happens next.
But then the second half came
I was also disappointed that instead of new open location we got just the recapitulation of the old one, with too much loot and a lot of enemies giving us too much green gel. That ment that I could upgrade almost everything to the max in just a few hours and as a result it became super easy. The ending sequence also dragged too long
for my taste... But even though it sounds very negative, it was still fun to play, but not at all as much as the first half, which was superior in almost every way.
Compared to the first TEW, I liked the first one more. Story in TEW2 has much better and clearer storytelling, but in the end I realised that the chaotic, not that clear story of the first TEW was more enjoyable, and thanks to it I had more reasons to replay it at least one more time. After completing TEW2, I feel like there is nothing more to find out and therefore not much reasons to give it another go. Visuals of the first TEW were also better. Most locations in TEW2 look really good, but some are so ugly I wanted to vomit.
So yeah... TEW2 is not as good as I hoped, mainly because of the second half of the game. First half is almost perfect. If it stayed like that until the end, it could easily outperform the first TEW, but they just didn't pull it off. It is still worth buying, but if you are expecting a sequel like Dead Space 2, you will probably be disappointed (but most people are happy with the entire game, so maybe it's just me...)

The gameplay is not revolutionary, and it will mostly consist of "move to new area, kill faceless bad guys, advance melodramatic plot."
And yet, for all of that, it remains fun, somehow. It's a junk food game. It's not going to make you reexamine war or its role in society, or whether we should give power-mad CEOs of PMCs unlimited power and cool technogical whizbang stuff (hint: that was a bad idea. It's always going to be a bad idea. Forever.). You won't walk away from it feeling like you had anything other than a moderately enjoyable experience...
But then again, isn't that why you're playing a COD game?

I was really on the fence with the first Evil Within, it had some really cool ideas and art direction but it was ultimately a disappointment for me but I did end up enjoying it. The Evil Within 2 is a step forward in a lot of was but also a bit of a step back.
I am currently about 10 hours into the game, so I haven't finished it yet. The Evil Within 2 improves on the combat of the first and gives players more options in terms of approaching combat. It is now easier to set traps, use stealth to pick off enemy's, and work with the environment to defeat threats. I choose to play the game on the hardest difficulty and that's the way it was meant to be played. However with more focus on the combat The Evil Within 2 loses much of the horror that the first game had. The Lost, the main enemy type in the game, are basically zombies and are not as interesting looking as the baddies in the first game. The special enemy types are more interesting then those in the first game, woman made from corpses with a saw blade arm is way more interesting then big guy with chainsaw. The enemy AI does a decent job but tend to give up the chase a little easy. Since they are all essentially zombies I wasn't expect much strategy from them, and they don't utilize strategy. The Evil Within 2 does a decent job of mixing up the combat with different enemy types. Some of the Lost will enter combat with Molotov cocktails in their hand that they will drop on death leaving a flaming area behind. There is a tougher female variant of the lost that comes into battle with a knife and they are both creepy and dangerous. There are also screamers, which are large twisted versions that have a ranged attack and can call in more of the smaller Lost. Finally there are some smaller lost that crawl on all fours and have the ability to move about the level more thanks to their increased agility. When the game is firing on all cylinders you will be swapping between weapons and strategies to manage the hordes. This is a lot of fun and works well, I really enjoyed approaching them moments in different ways. For example should I stealth kill the two on the edges and then back up to the roof of this building and snipe the screamer?
The Evil Within 2 also has boss fights that are less interesting then the mob fights. The bosses look great and their designs are both creepy and creative, but the way you fight them is very standard and easy. So far in the game I have fought three bosses one of which is a repeat of the first. On the hardest difficulty I have beaten each boss without taking any damage at all. Most of these fights devolve into run in circles shoot, run in circles. They are not unplayable or the worst thing ever but they are a little on the easy side and I would have enjoyed using more of my Grey matter and less of my reflexes in these moments.
Upgrades, upgrades, upgrades. The Evil Within 2 is filled with upgrades, upgrade parts, character upgrades, and ammo crafting. These things are really just part of the state of modern gaming, I have a hard time naming in game that came out in the last few years that doesn't have upgrade trees. The good news is that The Evil Within 2 awards exploration, you can find parts in the open areas that are valuable upgrade parts. Usually the rarer parts are hidden or guarded and presenting an entertaining challenge to get too.
Side quests, are present in the Evil Within 2 and for the most part they are really well done. They actually feel like they are part of the story and are more complex then just "go here get that." For me so far there haven't been a ton of sides quests but a few more focused ones, they feel essential to the game and skipping them would be a detriment to the experience.
Pc performance is ok but not great. I am running on a 980 and i7 4790k, on Ultra settings I usually maintain a 55-60 frame rate. It does drop often to a low of 45. I have tried running the game on low settings and the drops remain. They appear to be caused by some sort of bug in the Stem engine. The game isn't unplayable but depending on how forgiving you are, you may end up getting annoyed. For me it wasn't a big issue.
The biggest problem I have with the Evil Within 2 is the way in which Sebastian moves. His animations are odd and wonky. There are times when he glitches out or is animations break for a second or two. It just makes the game feel clunkier then it should. He also moves a little bit too slow while aiming, making back peddle shots more difficult.
The Evil Within 2 is a really fun time, and that's ultimately what matters in a game. I am having a blast with it and will be replaying the first game as soon as im done. I think that The Evil Within 2 could become a competitor to the Resident Evil series after another good game or two. The concept is cool and the general art direction and design is intriguing. I am excited for a third game. If Tango can improve this formula more for part three then we will be looking at GOTY material. I cant see the future of The Evil Within as a horror series but I cant see it as a merging of action and horror in the same vein as Resident Evil 4.
Bottom Line:
The Evil Within 2 reminds of a good John Carpenter movie. It mixes action with horror well, even if it does lose most of the horror after a few hours. The concept and world is creative and intriguing. The story is investing but not award winning. A great Halloween game and a fun experience. I recommend The Evil Within 2 to anyone who enjoyed the first game or The Last of Us. Now lets hope that Tango can improve the experience in part three, so we can have The Evil Within 3 GOTY edition.

Evil Within 1 at least had the trajectory of not knowing what is going on at first, then slowly piecing information together;  Evil Within 2 doesn't even have that. You're going to remember tense gameplay moments and emergent story, not anything anyone said. (I will say the story ramps up somewhat in the last third of the game, and I got a little more interested.)

I'm going to preface this review by letting you know that I am a big fan of positive, happy gaming experiences and that horror games, much like horror movies, are not my thing.  You need to know that so when I tell you that this game gave me everything I never thought I wanted out of horror gaming, you understand where I'm coming from.
Alien: Isolation was something of a nostalgia purchase for me.  I grew up with the Alien movies, and while I've never been a fan of scary stuff, I've always been frightfully curious about the appeal.  I've purchased other horror games, and given up when they were nothing but stock horror and jump scares.  They always came across as trite or desperate.  I bought Alien: Isolation hoping for something different, but expecting the same.
I was wrong.
Big picture, Alien: Isolation is an incredibly atmospheric game with a rich world set upon a space station the size of a city.  The ever-present danger the Alien represents, mixed with environmental, human, and android hazards was a great blend, forcing you to stay alert and aware for the tell-tale signs of the various threats.  Sometimes you only had to contend with one at a time, and sometimes combinations.  It was all blended together in a seamless dance that often had me hiding in a storage locker praying to god not to be found.
It's the little touches that really differentiated this game from other horror games for me.  Every other horror game I've played introduce the places you can hide right as you need them.  This game didn't.  Hiding places were everywhere, constant reminders that even when you weren't in danger, you could be.  Also, the stories put together from computer logs, of families separated and loved ones missing.  The increasingly falling apart space station, with damage and fires, graffitti and garbage piling up.  All of these things added to the terror of being hunted, a subtle note of sorrow and inevitability beneath the heart-pounding rush you get as you sprint for the emergency door over-ride to lock the pursuing Alien out of the room you just accidentally made a noise in.
I could go on and on about this game and all the things it does right.  The motion-tracker.  The crafting system.  The characters and the voice acting.  Atmosphere.  Story.  It's all really, really well done.
Overall, as someone who has a hard time with horror stuff, this game scared me in all the right places, in all the right ways.

This is not my type of game. I hate scary games but I still keep buying them. Why? Probably because Im border-line ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. However, as an 80's baby, movies like Alien and Predator are the centerpieces of my childhood. So, the nostalgia factor did weigh heavily on my decision to purchase this game. But Im glad that I did and I think there are some key points that set this game apart from other slow-paced, "thinking man's", digital scare-fest. Here is a list of some quick Pros and Cons. (tl;dr -> your mom)
Pros:
* Game looks great. (Even K-Putts SweetFx preset settings dont change much from the original)
* The construction of items works well with the story line. Other games make you build crap just because they need their lame game to be insteresting. Not the case here.
* There is a delicate balance of creepiness and the need to be cautious for tactical reasons.
* Devices and gadgets are great and they work well but not so well that it gives you too much of an advantage. Youre still screwed.
Cons:
* the combo of using multiple keys to use a tool is a bit strange and unecessarily cumbersome. It doesnt mess with gameplay (at least not yet). But to use you tool to cut a door brace requires holding both mouse buttons and then pressing a key. Why? Who thought that was a good idea?
* Running is a little slow and funky. With all of the other body movements being so darn good I wouldve expected to see the running follow suit.
* I wouldve preferred a true Aim Down Sights view. Im not a fan of the whatever it is that is being used (similar to Counterstrike or Half Life where the gun is always in front of you off to the side)

You play a guy with absolutely no fashion sense (jumpsuit and cybernetically implanted goggles make him look like Adam Jensen going through his goth phase) on his quest to find out just what went wrong on the Von Braun, which has seemingly been taken over by worm people and overly friendly robots who blow up in your face, spoiler alert. I've included a short version for those who don't want to do all this reading.
Short Version:
Pros:
-Excellent variety in weapons, the skill tree, and enemies
-Good hacking mechanic
-Good research mechanic
-Open-world
-Enemies dialog=chilling
-Excellent soundtrack
-Outdated graphics
Cons:
-Outdated graphics
-Animations in this game leave something to be desired
-Overly dramatic death animations from most enemies
-Researching could get annoying at times
Long Version:
While outdated, this game still has a lot to it.
The gameplay is extremely varied, from the number of different weapons you can get, to the psionic abilities, to skills. You can get different skills over time, and choose which of those skills to upgrade, allowing you to customize your character according to your playstyle. Your weapons get damaged over time, which means that you must perform maintenance on them periodically, which could get annoying at times. The hacking mechanic isn't as good as Bioshocks, but it's still very well done. The research function was a nice feature, which sometimes requires you to find the appropriate elements for your research. This could also get annoying, since you may be carrying around this or that slab of meat for a long time to find the correct chemical you need.
You can go almost anywhere in this game. You can return to earlier sections of the ship to look for stuff you might have missed or left, and all the different decks have their own unique style. There's a large variety of enemies, each with their own weaknesses and strengths, which you can learn about by researching their organs after you kill them. Most of the enemies you face are downright chilling, enhanced by the bad graphics. If you think you won't like this because of bad graphics, think again. The animations in this game are kind of bad, but that's to be expected in a game this old. One thing about the enemies I disliked though, is that once they were killed they had to have this long, dramatic death animation.
The game also has a terrific soundtrack and story, which really helps you get immersed in the game.
This game, is a true classic.

So a couple of days ago I got this game with the current discount that Steam offers (33% off) I thought frankly the game wasn't only incredibly badly optimized, but also it was a boring and dull experience, I didn't experience crashes or anything of the sort, but I did experience framedrops on the second mission during the infamous intro sequence as well as when staring down towards the city from the balcony.
I tried every setting imaginable and I just couldn't get a playable framerate, I tried everything I could, but for my standars, (which are high because I guess i'm a jerk) the game was just unplayable, it drop to the low 40 fps with some settings set to the lowest that they could get, in other cases the game just simply refused to stay above 30 fps, and so on and so forth, after having a confusing, and frustrating experience, I pretty much just refunded the game, that was of course until today.
I found a deal for the game at a "legit" website (according to a Bethesda representative that hangs around some forums on reddit) and whooptie doo, here we have my review. And I managed to fix my performance issues, How?
Welp...
i5 6600k
gtx 970
24 gb of ram
Those up there are my system specs, not to shabby, not to incredible, in my honest opinion, just a decent enough build.
I first disabled vsync completely, it turns out the input lag as well as the fact that it's the type of vsync that imposes double buffering, an uncommon form of applying vsync now a days, usually games use triple buffering without even telling you, to my understanding the simple rule of this to forms of vsync goes like this, double buffered locks your framerate at the half of your monitor's refresh rate, so if my monitor has an hz of 60, the game will simply lock my framerate to 30.
Triple buffering fixes this, but sadly it introduces an absurd amount of input lag, so the only solution for this was to disable vsync completely, something that both fixed in it's entirety the issue with the input lag, as well as the framerate issue, for the most part.
The second thing that I did was to set the game at the "default settings" meaning to have the game running at the recommended settings that the game offers based on my system specs.
It appears it set everything to the "medium" preset, the game looks good, nothing spectacular, nothing ugly, just good.
And... That's pretty much it, the game now runs and plays just fine, I just finished the first two levels and I felt the need to give a write up for this, maybe I experience problems at a later date, I hope not, but there.
DIshonored 2 as a game, when talking about the core, of the story, of the gameplay, of the actual experience, it's an absolute masterpiece so far, and i've put in maybe around two hours or so, with the first one being the one that made me slap my head and refund the game, and with the second one being one fueled by my curiosity as well as by my care for my limited income.
And i'm glad in all honesty that I purchased the game again, I really enjoy it, but that's not to say the game doesn't have it's fare share of problems, the game is plaguated by performance issues across all systems, for what i'm reading.
Maybe I could recommend it for people that don't mind dropping the settings down a bit, nor do other people that maybe don't mind playing the game at 30fps just like the rest of the platforms do, overall tho, I really hope they fix this on pc, because what i'm experiencing now, after a lot of trial an error, and just a lot of pacience and tolerance, is not what the regular buyer needs nor will it do, in most cases people will simply forget about the game and move along, and for a game that was clearly made with this much passion, with as much attention to detail, and with as much care, I frankly don't think it's fair, not to the consumer, and not to the creators themselves, to have them releasing this much of a broken mess.
Even then, i'm recommending it, because in my experience, is a great game, incredible really... If you can get it to play.

A very addictive, and surprisingly enjoyable game about cramming slimes in pens and selling their poop.
I am looking forward to future content updates, but I will go into a few suggestions that may or may not make be addressed later.
1. Add a breeding option with the slimes. Right now you can create a hybrid of two slimes, making a largo version with a combination of both traits. This is still interesting and useful, but I feel some complexity could be added by allowing a way to "create" new slimes, even if it was just a fancy machine that took two slimes and makes a third if it was one of the preselected pairings.
2. Automation. I read that this is part of a future content patch, but this was the biggest concern for me. I wanted to explore, but I felt like I had to spend a great deal of my time picking up crops, feeding slimes, and selling plorts. Automating this doesn't have to mean removing these steps, but apart from the plort collector, many of the upgrades don't make the individual tasks easier.
3. More complexity in the market. Right now it seems if you sell plorts on one day, it will go down in price the next. Sell more the next day and it will drop further until it hits a baseline value. If you ignore a market, the prices go back up. This makes sense if the goal is to force diverse ranching to keep up profits. Instead, the "best" option I saw is to stockpile plorts of a given type until the market is high, sell them all, then ignore the market until it maxes out again. A market that fluctuates more outside of your control, or is more resiliant to just a few sales might make for a better system.
4. Faster energy regeneration. Too often I am trying to explore new areas and I just have to sit around for a few seconds while my energy regen kicks in. Maybe make it start earlier if there are no slimes or dangers around.

Cute but shallow; the gameplay in its current state is virtually identical to the way it was at early access launch, though now it features a few (one or two?) more shallow, linear areas and a couple more slimes.
The game consists entirely of sucking up slimes, sticking them in a pen, feeding them their favored food (fruit, vegetables, or meat), and then selling their plorts. You use the money from selling their plorts to buy more pens to hold more slimes, or more areas to hold more pens to hold more slimes, and though they all behave a little bit differently, and look different, it's effectively the same exact thing every time you do it.
You can also grow the food for your slimes, but it consists of simply sticking chickens in a pen, where they automatically multiply, or a fruit into a field, where it immediately grows into a tree and spawns fruit every day.
The game very quickly becomes tedious, as none of this can be automated, so once you've gotten all your slimes penned (takes less than 30 minutes) and your food planted/penned, you could theoretically just sleep every day away, go gather all your slime food, stick it in the pen autofeeder, sell the plorts, and then sleep again. There's nothing pushing you to do more than that, and nothing to see even if you do. All the areas in the game are just big empty linear pathways where slimes hop around eating whatever they can fit into their mouths, waiting to be sucked up and stuck in a pen by you. Sometimes they turn into weird goo monsters and kill all the other slimes until they themselves die, and then more slimes just pop out of the ground, so none of it matters.
It's kind of a bummer, but whatever, it's not like there isn't Stardew Valley, Rune Factory, Story of Seasons, and two decades of Harvest Moon games to play instead. Hell, even that garbage heap Innocent Life is a better game than this.

First, I've been a huge fan of the (original) King's Quest series since I was a child and learned to read and use the computer while sitting on my father's lap playing KQ1.
I checked 3 times upon starting that I wasn't missing some intro or something. When you start chapter 1 it feels like you're interrupting a story already in progress with no context as to why you're there or what you're doing. You're just young Graham standing on a path.  Well that's fine, but then you continue on and there's comments made about a treasure and looking for something. What that is you have no idea because it doesn't tell you anywhere.  The narrator is also talking to someone and you don't know who that is. Now after going and watching some of the trailers for the game, and reading on the forums, You can find these answers, but that's hardly conducive to an immersive gaming experience.
The other issue is that the game feels more like you're watching a cartoon (one that you have to hold down a single button to make it continue) rather than playing an actual game. There's no real challenges or choices thus far.  Granted only half the game has been released, and I've only done 1 chapter so far, but I'm already feeling cheated. This game has the same characters and some of the same humour, but none of the real challenges or fantastic adventure feeling found in the original series.
I'll ammend this review if the above changes with subsequent chapters. I really hope it does because I want to love this game.

The Elder Scrolls Online (ESO) is Bethesda’s and Zenimax’s attempt at a multiplayer Elder Scrolls game. ESO received average review scores since launch and after about a year and half the game has received some much needed updates. Below I will provide a score between 1 and 10 rating different aspects* of the game.
9/10
ESO is a huge open world with 3 factions, 4 classes, and 10 different races to play as (if you buy the Imperial Edition you get access to the Imperial race). Factions, classes, and races each have their own unique traits so you don’t have to worry about your lack of character customization. If you were a fan of Skyrim, Oblivion, or any of the Elder Scroll games you probably played in first person because that’s how the games were intended to be played in. ESO has both first and third person. I spend most of my time in the third person and I would say that it’s more enjoyable that way. Sadly there are no slow motion decapitation scenes like there was in Skyrim but that is expected since the game has to appeal to as many audiences possible. The MMO hack and slash style is very well implemented and feels rewarding. You can have a total of 8 ability slots, 2 ultimate’s and as many passives as you want. In ESO you will be battling multiple enemies at once so you need to spend your mana and stamina wisely and kill the most threatening enemies first. PVP is absolutely exhilarating. Battling with hundreds of players, whether they are faction members or enemies, and fighting for control over a Keep is some of the most fun you will have in a video game.
8.5/10
Out of the many MMOs I have played, ESO has the best graphics by far. Of course the graphics are not on par with games like Battlefront but the detail that goes into the world is stunning for an MMO. The game world has many types of terrains. For example icy mountains, deserts, forests, grasslands etc. ESO does copy many building assets so it can get repetitive going inside different buildings but there is always some loot to find whether it’s lame like coffee or some sweet gear. It rarely gets boring just exploring the world of Tamriel. There are always new and interesting places to find.
10/10
ESO allows the player to download add-ons to “enhance” their game. There are tons of add-ons to download like map, inventory, spell, data, pvp, and raid add-ons just to list a few. Add-ons are extremely helpful in finding things like quests, sky shards, lore books, undiscovered locations, or seeing your damage dealt. In general add-ons help improve the gameplay drastically.
6/10 (minus 4 points)
There are not many problems that I found with ESO but that ones that were really annoying I will list below.
-Download size: can take an extremely long time if you have trash internet.
-Leveling: XP gain is very slow. For example I’m 40 hours in and my character is only level 30.
-Only group with friends from the same faction.
-Mount Cost: Absolutely insane. Can take a long time to save up for 42,000 gold.
-Mount bug still in game
-Ping in general is too high
-Occasional lag spikes in alliance pvp zones
8.4/10
ESO is one of the very few MMO’s I will highly recommend. Every minute of my time spent in the game has been an absolute blast. Whether you are playing solo or with friends, ESO is a must buy especially if it’s on sale.

Explosive, hilarious, and just down right fun. Broforce brings you into a world of massive patriotism and enemies galore. Pixaleted platforming, gunplay and co-op along with some nicely implemented workshop features, allows the game to have seemingly endless amounts of fun.
I had tons of fun dying over and over, laughing at the comical moments that occurred all around me. Hell even the most basic enemy in the game would occasionally get a good shot in and send me to my grave. Never once did I get frustrated, as it was always my own fault. Soon after dying 20+ times you'll stumble upon an amazing run that ends the previously difficult level in a matter of seconds, furthering the feeling of being a complete dummy with the quick realization that you really do suck sometimes.
Along the way you'll gain access to more troops to play as. Each one being its own humorous parody of a well-known character. Not only are they recognizable by many, but they also have their own individual weaponry and skills.
If you're looking for a fast paced and enjoyable game, I cannot recommend Broforce enough. It simply is just gaming fun at the most barebones level, and I love it.

This is the first horror game I have actually enjoyed playing. Usually, horror games are played for the sake of being scared whereas this game isn't. The reason this game is better than normal horrors, is because it isn't focused on scaring, there is an actual point of doing everything. Rather than just entering a haunted forest becasue "Why Not?" you enter the room where the Alien is because there is something you have to do which depends on everyone's lives.
Also there are some really nice, clever game mechanics (like the hacking and holding your breath, etc.). There is a lot of attention to detail in this game aswell (Tracker can randomly lose connection, Alien can hear tracker beeping, Alien can eventually realise that noisemakers and flares are fake and just distractions, etc.).
The story is absouloutly brilliant. It has the same atmosphere form the movies where NOTHING EVER GOES RIGHT! I get the feeling that my current objective in the game isn't going to work. DON'T, I mean DON'T watch any videos of the story. This game is so much better spoiler free. I have watched a few videos on certain points of the game and I completely regret it. Seriously DON'T watch videos.
Haven't played the DLCs myself but judging by the descriptions, I thing I really am going to. Two of them are from parts of the original film by Ridley Scott and I look foward to playing them once I have completed the story.
Overall, a really decent game. Although I hate the horror genre, this is in my top 3 games (those being; Elite: Dangerous, Alien: Isolation, and Grand Theft Auto 5). This Game comepletely deserves it's game of the year award and I would reccomend it to Alien fans and horror fans, and even those who love a good story.

Well...
This was...a thing. That I played.
I've heard a lot about how good this game is. And how it's just as good as other OW survival games like H1Z1 or Rust.
And when I started it up I was already disappointed. No character customization or choice, for that matter. We're all just a bunch of clones of the same dude, running around trying to kill each other.
Graphically, it's nice, especially for an alpha game.
Kind of reminded me of The Long Dark, which is a very beautiful game.
But not even a minute in, some naked a$$hole asked if i had any tools, (a lot of newbs do this) and I just said nah, that I just started and parted ways. And what does this guy do? He comes up behind me, fully dressed and with a bow and arrow-and shoots me in the back.
That. Is the PVP community. So if you can't even begin to tolerate that, games like this aren't for you. Because no single player mode. Because who would EVER play this kind fo game and not want immature and bigoted public in it? Because zero moderation. They could just camp all day there and shoot anyone that spawns. Plus no screening for a$$holes- the same issue I had with H1Z1, who are solely a PVP/PVE game.
And pf. Good luck finding a server that is PVE. They don't even have an official one. And if they do, they certainly don't label it. Nor do the admins (or anyone) will answer you on if it is or isn't. I most certainly didn't feel welcome on every server I tried.
They won't even answer you if you ask why the hell the servers are wiped every two weeks.
And yeah, it seems like every server does it. So anyone in this game for the long haul? If you can weight five or six years, they'll have it for you. But right now, it's a game where you ♥♥♥♥ around for an hour before you get bored. Because there's no point exploring their world if all your hard work disappears every 16 days. Not to mention most of what I saw for a map, there wasn't nearly enough content. There's a deadzone of desert the size of Texas running through the split of the map.
And WHILE I UNDERSTAND this is an alpha game, and wipes will happen every once in awhile. I fully expect that without much issue...But every two weeks???
That's ridiculous and outraging.
Do you even know about your demographic? Open world survivalists want a long time to live in the world. We want to explore the fullest levels and skill you can accomplish. We want to build as much as we want without a damned deadline. And sure we appreciate frequent updating...but not so much that you break the game.
So now, it's just a game in my library which I wistfully sigh at, before moving on to another alpha OWS that actually functions enough to at least spend $16 on it.
TLDR- This game will be pretty damned cool once it's playable. Would give a 3/10 right now, and can't recommend until they improve.
